Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time includes the imitative play through which young learn knapping; the longer reduction sequences of bifacial technology require extended practice, and play-knapping becomes a significant component of sociability.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Stratification remains minimal; skilled knappers may enjoy informal status, but there is no formalized hierarchy, and leadership remains situational.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; the band is self-organizing, with decision-making ad hoc and consensus-based.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: There is no organized coercive capacity; violence is interpersonal, and the group lacks any monopoly on force.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is low; the cooperative demands of Acheulean learning may actually reduce conflict by creating mutual dependencies between generations.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal, exercised by skilled knappers and successful foragers; authority derives from demonstrated competence rather than formal office.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to the band as a survival and learning unit; belonging is immediate and affective, not abstracted into political legitimacy.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective will coalesces around immediate challenges; there is no sustained political project, and resolve is episodic.

External Relations & Posture: Inter-band relations are unknown; the sparse population suggests infrequent contact, and posture toward outsiders is likely cautious.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The prevailing mood is shaped by daily subsistence rhythms; trust extends to band members, and the demands of cooperative learning may foster patience and tolerance as social norms.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection is not legible at this scale; the affective life is immediate, and collective exhaustion does not accumulate as a standing condition.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is gestural, vocal, and demonstrative but pre-linguistic; the complexity of Acheulean knapping suggests refined gestural communication, with experts guiding novice hands through multi-step sequences.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of direct demonstration; the longer reduction sequences require sustained attention and repeated observation, slowing transmission velocity but increasing fidelity within dyads.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No record exists; knowledge persists only in living memory and skilled hands, with the finished handaxe itself serving as a kind of frozen demonstration of the technique that produced it.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: There is no framing apparatus; what can be communicated is limited by the expressive capacity of gesture and the observer's ability to parse complex action sequences.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is face-to-face; Acheulean learning demands sustained focus from novice observers, selecting for individuals capable of extended attentional investment.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity in direct transmission is high, but the imitative mode introduces drift; slight variations in technique accumulate across generations, producing regional variants visible in the archaeological record.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The moral sense remains proto-ethical, grounded in expectations of sharing and reciprocity; the patience required to teach and learn Acheulean knapping may reinforce norms of tolerance and forbearance.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: There is no law; conduct is regulated by expectation and immediate consequence, not by codified rule.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved through confrontation or avoidance; there is no adjudicating body, and sanction is personal rather than systematic.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Rights do not exist as a category; individuals are protected by kinship and band membership, not by formal entitlement.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed immediately or not at all; there is no accumulating deficit of justice.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no formal inquiry; understanding is practical and procedural, embedded in the action of knapping itself, with no separation of knowing from doing.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Acheulean knapping constitutes the technical method: selecting appropriate blanks, planning reduction sequences, maintaining symmetry across multiple removals, and recognizing when a tool is finished; this is a significantly more demanding cognitive and motor sequence than Oldowan technology, requiring extended imitative learning to master.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is entirely imitative; novices learn by watching experts and practicing under guidance, hand correcting hand; the knowledge stock is what living practitioners can demonstrate, and skill distribution varies by individual aptitude and learning opportunity.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge remains vulnerable to transmission failure; if skilled practitioners die before transmitting, techniques may be lost, and the imitative mode introduces drift that can degrade precision over generations.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no narrative mythos; identity is immediate, grounded in band membership and the shared practice of tool-making, with no story of origins or collective memory extending beyond living experience.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists; the order requires no justification because alternatives are inconceivable.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is functional, but the symmetry and regularity of the Acheulean handaxe suggest an emerging aesthetic dimension; the form exceeds strict functional requirements, implying that makers attended to shape as a value in itself.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: There is no cultural form to exhaust; meaning is procedural and instrumental, and no symbolic residue accumulates, though the handaxe's persistence as a form over hundreds of thousands of years suggests a deep conservatism rather than exhaustion.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: There is no detectable cosmology; the hominin mind at this stage may not frame existential questions in ways that would leave material traces.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual is attested; behavior remains instrumental, and devotional practice, if any, leaves no trace.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists; there is no clergy, no doctrine, no authority over the sacred.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: There is no spiritual system to diffuse or displace; the category does not apply.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment presupposes enchantment; here the sacred has not yet emerged as a differentiated category, and there is no residue of lost transcendence.

docs.title: 350,000 BCE – 200,000 BCE — Late Acheulean to Middle Stone Age Transition
docs.text: Summary: A long-term trend across the Northwest African littoral and Atlas margins in which the Classic Acheulean bifacial tradition gives way to prepared-core (Levallois) flaking technologies that yield standardized flakes and points rather than handaxes; the binding constraint remains the imitative mode of transmission, which permits gradual drift and local innovation but cannot accelerate diffusion or arrest regression, so the transition unfolds unevenly across space and time without any possibility of codified instruction or recorded precedent.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The transition plays out across the Atlantic Moroccan coast, from Casablanca southward through the Doukkala plain, and inland along the flanks of the Middle and High Atlas; the coastal strand offers low-friction movement, while the mountain valleys channel and constrain interior travel.

Climate Regime & Volatility: Marine Isotope Stages 9 through 7 (roughly 330,000–190,000 years ago) bring alternating humid and arid phases; humid intervals open Saharan corridors connecting the Maghreb to sub-Saharan populations, while arid intervals contract habitable range toward coastal and montane refugia.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Drought is the principal hazard, capable of collapsing local carrying capacity; the Atlantic moderates coastal aridity, but interior populations face sharper oscillations; no volcanic or major seismic hazard impinges on the region during this window.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Flint and quartzite remain available in marine-terrace deposits and stream gravels; the shift toward Levallois technique does not require new raw materials but exploits existing nodules more efficiently, yielding more usable edge per unit of stone.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Lithic debitage continues to accumulate at reduction sites; environmental impact remains negligible at prevailing population densities; sink capacity is not a limiting factor.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic disease load persists without major epidemic signature; mortality from trauma, infection, and nutritional stress continues to shape population turnover, but no new pathogen regime emerges.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Access to diverse fauna and coastal resources supports adequate nutrition; body size and robusticity remain high, though climatic oscillations periodically stress provisioning.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Wound care and nursing remain within-group, transmitted by observation; there is no advance in healing technique discernible from the archaeological record.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Cooperative breeding and extended juvenile dependency continue; no change in reproductive biology is detectable, though population structure may shift as groups expand or contract with climate.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population remains sparse and fluctuates with climate; humid phases likely see expansion into previously marginal areas, while arid phases concentrate survivors in refugia; replacement ratios hover near parity.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: The dependency load remains light; group mobility constrains the survival of those unable to travel; short-term support of the injured is possible, but chronic dependency is unsustainable.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Immediate-return foraging continues; the transition to Levallois technology may improve hunting efficiency through standardized, hafted points, but the subsistence mode remains unaltered.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle remains the sole prime mover; fire is in routine use; no new energy source is captured during the transition.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Division of labor remains informal; the new reduction technique is more demanding of planning and sequential control, possibly concentrating production among fewer skilled practitioners.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Levallois technique is more economical of raw material than bifacial shaping, extracting more cutting edge per nodule; this efficiency may buffer against raw-material scarcity but does not generate storable surplus.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No formal storage technology emerges; caches of prepared cores or blanks at favored sites may represent proto-reserves, but evidence is ambiguous.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange remains face-to-face and reciprocal; there is no evidence of long-distance trade networks; raw-material transport is limited to what individuals carry.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of exchange or unit of account exists; obligations are tracked through memory and repaid in kind.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Redistribution continues through immediate sharing; no institutionalized extraction emerges.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Personal possessions remain minimal; a toolkit, body knowledge, and social standing constitute individual wealth; defense is situational.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Lithic debitage is left at reduction sites; organic waste decays; no environmental load accumulates.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Small bands persist as the basic social unit; kinship ties structure cooperation and resource sharing; inheritance remains experiential, passed through imitation.

Association & Mutual Aid: Cooperative hunting, shared childcare, and mutual defense continue; the increased cognitive demand of Levallois reduction may favor tighter apprentice-expert relationships within the band.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Play and grooming maintain social bonds; communal rest follows foraging; no new sociability structures emerge.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status remains fluid, tied to demonstrated competence; mastery of the new reduction technique may confer additional prestige to skilled knappers.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; coordination is achieved through imitation and situational leadership.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Hafted points may improve hunting weaponry, but organized coercion remains absent; disputes are settled by dominance, avoidance, or fission.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Friction dissipates through band fission; the small-group scale keeps grievance personal and manageable.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership remains situational; mastery of the cognitively demanding Levallois technique may concentrate authority among a smaller set of expert knappers whose competence is directly witnessed.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance attaches to individuals whose competence and generosity are visibly demonstrated; no institutional legitimacy exists.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is mobilized through shared affect and imitative entrainment; no verbal deliberation is possible; resolve is achieved by visible consensus.

External Relations & Posture: Encounters with other bands remain cautious; mutual assessment precedes interaction; avoidance is the default response to strangers.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Group cohesion depends on face-to-face familiarity; sentiment fluctuates with provisioning success and climatic conditions; humid phases may foster expansion and optimism, arid phases caution and contraction.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection expresses itself through departure; the option of fission dissipates accumulated grievance before it crystallizes into chronic conflict.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication rests on gesture, posture, vocalization, and facial expression; no articulate language is available; mutual legibility requires prolonged co-presence.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of bodily movement; the reach of any message is limited to those within sight or earshot; innovations spread only as fast as their practitioners move.

Record, Storage & Persistence: There is no external record; all knowledge resides in living heads; the Levallois technique, once mastered, persists only as long as its practitioners live and demonstrate it to successors.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: No discursive framing exists; there is no conceptual censorship, only the implicit constraint of what can be shown.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is directed by pointing, gaze, and physical guidance; amplification occurs only through repeated demonstration to successive learners.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Each transmission drifts; without a fixed record to correct against, cumulative drift can simplify or alter technique over generations; the prepared-core concept is robust to drift because the core itself serves as a physical template for the next stage of reduction.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Reciprocity remains the operative principle; sharing is expected and free-riding punished by exclusion; no codified ethic exists.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No formal law exists; behavioral norms are implicit in practice and enforced through social consequence.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved situationally; there is no institutionalized adjudication; avoidance and fission substitute for formal sanction.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is constrained only by group pressure; no formal rights are recognized.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongdoing beyond group tolerance results in exclusion; chronic impunity is limited by small-group scale and the impossibility of anonymity.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry exists; understanding is procedural, embedded in the motor sequences of tool production and foraging routines.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: The Levallois reduction sequence represents a cognitive advance: the knapper must envision the final flake before removing it, shaping the core to predetermine the product's size and shape; this requires greater planning depth than bifacial shaping and produces standardized, often hafted, flakes and points with predictable morphology.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Skill transmission remains imitative; the increased complexity of prepared-core reduction may narrow the cohort who achieve mastery, concentrating advanced technique among fewer hands; the knowledge stock is the sum of what living practitioners carry.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: When a master knapper dies without demonstrating the full reduction sequence, elements of the technique may be lost; local populations can regress to simpler methods if transmission is interrupted; there is no record to preserve the technique against such loss.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Group identity remains grounded in shared experience; there is no narrative mythos, only embodied memory of places, faces, and repeated actions.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No ideological justification for the social order exists; the order is the way things are done, validated by imitation of predecessors.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: The prepared core and its products display a different aesthetic than the Acheulean handaxe: symmetry is now in the flake rather than the core, and standardization suggests a shared mental template; the transition alters the material-culture signature without introducing symbolic elaboration.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Cultural forms remain unelaborated symbolically; the new technique does not exhaust but rather supplements the repertoire, and both traditions may coexist locally during the transition.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No articulate cosmology is possible without language; the world is encountered directly; the subject's place in it is unreflected.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: If proto-ritual exists, it is indistinguishable from habitual action; no deliberate symbolic behavior is attested during this window.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists; spiritual authority is meaningless in the absence of communicable doctrine.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: There is nothing to diffuse; belief in the conceptual sense does not yet exist.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment presupposes prior enchantment; the category does not apply; the spiritual dimension remains latent, awaiting the emergence of language and symbolic thought.

docs.title: 250,000 BCE – 150,000 BCE — Middle Stone Age Establishment in the Maghreb
docs.text: Summary: Across the northwestern corner of Africa, populations carrying Middle Stone Age technology occupy coastal terraces, interior valleys, and highland margins, producing Levallois flakes and points that mark a cognitive and technical advance over earlier Acheulean industries. The binding constraint remains the imitative stage: prepared-core knapping, knowledge of seasonal resources, and whatever social conventions govern this dispersed population persist only through direct demonstration and copying, hand guiding hand. No message outlasts its carrier; no instruction survives its demonstrator. This snapshot captures the established baseline of Middle Stone Age lifeways before the Aterian cultural florescence, a period of regional adaptation and slow technique refinement within the narrow channel that imitative transmission permits.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Maghreb encompasses the Atlantic Moroccan littoral, the Tell Atlas of Algeria, the High and Middle Atlas ranges, and the northern Saharan fringe. The coastal strip offers marine resources and moderate climate; the Atlas ranges create elevational zonation from Mediterranean scrubland to montane forest; the interior steppe transitions to desert. Movement along the coast is relatively unimpeded; cross-Atlas travel requires negotiating passes. The Strait of Gibraltar narrows to 14 kilometers, occasionally permitting contact with Iberia during low sea-stands.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The window spans multiple climatic oscillations, from humid phases enabling Saharan penetration to arid phases contracting habitable range toward coastal refugia. Marine Isotope Stages 7 and 6 (~245-130 ka) bring alternating warm-humid and cold-dry conditions. Atlantic influence moderates the northwestern coast; interior regions experience greater extremes. Secular trend is toward increasing aridity with punctuated humid episodes. Populations must track these shifts through mobility or face local extinction.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Seismic activity along the Atlas fault system produces periodic ground-shaking and landslides. Flash flooding in seasonal wadis threatens camps during rare but intense rainfall. Drought and heat waves stress populations during arid phases. Wildfire, whether natural or anthropogenic, periodically sweeps scrubland and forest. The primary buffer is mobility — populations relocate rather than endure. Margin is adequate during humid phases, thin during arid ones.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Flint, quartzite, and other knappable stone outcrop across the region, with quality varying by locality. Water sources range from perennial Atlantic-fed streams to seasonal wadis dependent on rainfall regime. Fauna includes gazelle, hartebeest, zebra, and various bovids in grassland zones; forest margins support deer and boar; coastal zones offer shellfish, fish, and marine mammals. Plant resources vary by biome and season. The endowment is adequate but patchily distributed, requiring mobility and landscape knowledge.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Population densities remain very low throughout the window. Organic waste disperses and decomposes; lithic debitage accumulates at knapping stations without ecological consequence. Fire releases carbon but at negligible scale. The sink is nowhere near saturation; no anthropogenic degradation is detectable. The residue is nil in ecological terms, archaeologically productive as preserved sites.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic parasites, zoonotic infections, and periodic epidemic events maintain a mortality baseline elevated above modern standards. Malaria may affect humid lowland zones; intestinal parasites are ubiquitous. Wound infection following hunting injuries or interpersonal violence claims some fraction of the population. The trend is stable within the window; no catastrophic epidemic is evidenced, though absence of evidence constrains certainty.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Skeletal evidence from this window is sparse, but the persistence and spread of Middle Stone Age populations implies adequate nutrition on average. Body size and robusticity suggest sufficient protein and caloric intake during favorable phases. Dental wear indicates mixed diet. Periodic nutritional stress during arid phases may elevate mortality without leaving skeletal traces in survivors. The baseline is adequacy, not abundance.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing depends on the body's regenerative capacity plus whatever wound-tending, bone-setting, and herbal application the group practices — transmitted entirely by demonstration. No systematic medicine exists; care is personal and kin-based. Survival of significant injury is possible, as earlier Jebel Irhoud evidence shows, but capacity is limited to what can be shown and copied. Recovery from serious illness or injury is uncertain.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Homo sapiens reproductive biology is fully established: extended juvenile dependency, high parental investment, flexible pair-bonding, and concealed ovulation. Fertility is physiologically adequate; realized reproduction depends on provisioning success and infant survival. Selective pressure continues to favor cognitive and social capacity. Mating patterns are unknowable but likely variable across populations.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density averages perhaps one person per hundred square kilometers or less across the habitable zone, clustering at resource concentrations. Band sizes likely range from 15 to 40 individuals. Replacement is near zero or slightly positive during favorable phases; local extinctions probably occur during severe arid phases. Migration flows connect populations across the region, preventing complete isolation. The demographic structure is stable at low density.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: The extended juvenile period creates a standing dependency load. Elderly individuals who survive to old age become knowledge repositories but also provisioning burdens. The productive cohort absorbs this load during favorable conditions. During resource stress, the very young and very old bear elevated mortality risk. The residue is the biological cost of the sapiens life-history strategy — cleared when surplus permits, accumulating as mortality when it does not.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Hunting and gathering provide all subsistence. Large game hunting using hafted stone points represents the primary protein source in most zones; coastal populations exploit shellfish and possibly fish and marine mammals. Plant foods — tubers, seeds, fruits, nuts — provide carbohydrates and micronutrients seasonally. The provisioning floor sits above starvation during humid phases but may compress during arid periods, requiring range expansion or dietary broadening.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Fire is universally controlled and used for cooking, warmth, tool-hardening, and possibly landscape management. Human muscle provides all productive work. The per-capita energy ceiling is set by human physiology and the efficiency of technique. No animal or mechanical power is harnessed. Energy throughput is low but adequate for subsistence and the modest surplus required for reproduction.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor organization is task-based and flexible. All capable adults participate in provisioning activities appropriate to age, sex, and condition. Specialization beyond this is minimal and situational. Coercion is limited to social pressure expressed through demonstrated approval or disapproval. Children learn by watching and assisting adults; instruction is entirely imitative. No formal labor hierarchy exists.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production consists of tool manufacture, food acquisition, shelter construction, and fire maintenance. The Middle Stone Age toolkit — Levallois cores, points, scrapers — represents increased standardization and efficiency over Acheulean predecessors. Surplus above immediate consumption is ephemeral: a successful hunt provides temporary abundance; gatherable plant foods are consumed or lost within days. No durable surplus accumulates.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No technology for long-term storage exists. Body fat provides individual reserves; landscape diversity provides collective insurance through mobility. A local failure is absorbed by moving to better-provisioned areas. Risk-pooling is social — sharing within the band — but no material buffer persists between seasons. The margin against shock is the range of accessible territory and the knowledge of fallback resources.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is immediate and reciprocal within the band. Delayed reciprocity extends only as far as personal memory tracks. Raw materials are procured locally where possible; occasional transport of good-quality stone over tens of kilometers suggests some inter-group contact, but systematic trade networks are not evidenced. Logistics is carrying capacity on foot. The home range is whatever area can be traversed seasonally.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No abstract value-store or unit of account exists. Obligation is tracked in memory: who gave, who received, who owes. Credit is the expectation that sharing will be reciprocated when fortunes reverse. This implicit accounting cannot be externalized; it lives only in heads. Deferred exchange is personal debt, not transferable or enforceable beyond social pressure.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: No extraction apparatus exists; redistribution is voluntary sharing. A successful hunter shares meat with kin and allies according to social expectation, not formal requirement. The "tax" is the expectation of future sharing in return. No tribute flows to a ruling stratum; no rent is paid for access to resources. The surplus flow is horizontal among near-equals, not vertical.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Material wealth consists of portable tools, gathered resources, and personal knowledge. Nothing durable accumulates; concentration is structurally impossible. Defense consists of carrying one's tools, remembering one's caches, and maintaining the social ties that ensure sharing access. The Gini coefficient, were it measurable, would approach zero. The residue is the broken and discarded — archaeologically informative, economically negligible.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste is left at camps and processed by decomposition and scavenging. Lithic waste accumulates at knapping stations and processing sites. Neither stream requires management; the environment absorbs all output without saturation. Fire produces smoke and ash, dispersed by wind and rain. No pollution accumulates; no cleanup is required. The residue is nil.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship structures the band. Nuclear families within extended kin networks form the daily living unit. Inheritance is biological — children inherit nothing but genes and whatever they can learn by watching. Marriage or pair-bonding practices are unknowable but likely involve recognition of kin relationships and some form of incest avoidance. The scaffold of obligation follows biological connection.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band of 15-40 individuals is the primary association. Mutual aid is obligatory among kin, expected among co-residents. Hunting parties, child-minding arrangements, and food-sharing networks structure cooperation. There are no formal organizations, guilds, or institutions — only the informal fabric of kin and residential ties. This fabric is the sole social insurance; there is nothing beyond it.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in rest, sociability, grooming, and play. Children's play rehearses adult activities through imitation. Adults engage in social interaction, storytelling (to whatever extent pre-linguistic vocalization permits), and perhaps dance or rhythmic activity. Shared meals are social occasions. Sociability maintains the bonds on which survival depends.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status is informal, earned through demonstrated competence, age, and success. The best hunter, the most knowledgeable elder, the most attractive mate hold higher status, but this translates into deference and imitation, not material accumulation or formal authority. Boundaries between groups are permeable; individuals may transfer through mating or fission. No rigid stratification exists; inequality is personal and situational.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administration exists. Decisions are made by consensus, deference to experience, or individual initiative. There are no offices, no bureaucracy, no procedures. Record-keeping is impossible; coordination is face-to-face. Capacity is limited to what can be accomplished by direct interaction within the band. Anything requiring institutional memory or complex coordination is simply not possible.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: No organized coercive capacity exists beyond the capacity of individuals and small groups. Weaponry consists of hunting implements — hafted points, wooden spears — which serve equally for violence. No fortification or military organization exists. The balance of force is rough equality among adult males; none can systematically coerce others. Violence, where it occurs, is personal and reciprocal.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is discharged through avoidance, fission, and departure. Grievance that cannot be resolved through reconciliation leads to spatial separation — individuals or families leaving to join other bands. Crime as a concept does not apply at band scale; wrongdoing is personal and addressed personally. The residue is the friction that departure does not resolve — interpersonal animosity carried until death, occasional violent resolution.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational and earned. The experienced tracker leads the hunt; the elder with landscape knowledge guides seasonal movement. Authority derives from demonstrated competence, not formal position. Charisma — the ability to attract attention and imitation — matters for influence. No permanent leaders exist; authority shifts with task and circumstance.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to kin and band, not to abstract authority or institution. Compliance follows from trust in demonstrated competence, not from belief in a right to rule. Disaffection manifests as reduced cooperation and eventual departure. Legitimacy is personal and continuously renegotiated through daily interaction. There is no regime to legitimize or delegitimize — only relationships.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action requires assembling individual wills in real time. The decision to move, to hunt, to confront a threat emerges from interaction, not from command. There is no standing political will or institutional capacity for sustained action. Mobilization is ad hoc; resolve lasts as long as immediate motivation persists. The struggle for influence is the competition for attention and imitation.

External Relations & Posture: Relations between bands range from intermarriage and cooperation to avoidance and conflict, depending on kinship connections and resource competition. Expansion is simply occupation of unoccupied territory during favorable conditions. There is no formal diplomacy; relationships are personal. Conflict, where it occurs, is between individuals or small groups, not organized warfare.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The emotional life of Middle Stone Age Maghrebian populations is inaccessible, but the structure of small-group living implies high mutual familiarity and trust calibrated by repeated interaction. Anxiety focuses on immediate threats: predators, hunger, injury, conflict. The behavioral temper is cautious, alert to danger, attentive to social cues. Trust extends throughout the band and to known individuals in neighboring bands; beyond that, strangers are approached with wariness.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Exhaustion from hardship, grief from loss, and frustration from conflict can drain individual and collective will. Chronic failure may lead to apathy and social withdrawal. The discharge mechanism is mobility — the demoralized can leave or rest. The residue is whatever malaise and distrust persist in individuals or groups unable to act — absorbed through time or carried to death.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: The imitative stage constrains communication to demonstration, gesture, vocalization, and bodily imitation. No fully symbolic language exists. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band, where long familiarity creates shared gestural and vocal conventions, but may fail across populations without sustained contact. The code is embodied, learned by watching, and inherently local. Anything that cannot be shown cannot be communicated.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of physical proximity. Voice carries meters; gesture requires line-of-sight. No channel extends beyond immediate presence. News does not precede its carrier; messages cannot be sent ahead. The reach is the band's daily range; beyond that, information stops unless someone walks it there.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists. All knowledge is held in living memory and transmitted by demonstration. When knowledge-holders die without successful imitators, their knowledge dies with them. Fidelity depends on the copier's attention and ability; drift accumulates with each transmission. The archaeological record preserves artifacts but not the knowledge used to make them. Nothing survives except what is copied.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Without symbolic language, discourse norms exist only as conventions about who may demonstrate what to whom. Social attention governs information flow: the young watch the old, the novice watches the expert. Taboo, where it exists, is transmitted by aversive response rather than verbal prohibition. The permitted band is whatever can be demonstrated and accepted.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is the scarce resource. Information propagates when it captures attention and is successfully copied. A useful technique spreads through the band as each member watches and imitates. Amplification is repeated demonstration. Reception depends on proximity, relationship, and the capacity to observe and replicate. Nothing goes viral in a population this sparse.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Every transmission introduces variation — the copier's interpretation of what was demonstrated. No mechanism exists for verification against an original; no original persists independently. Signal integrity depends on redundancy and correction through repeated observation. Noise accumulates across generations. The residue is cumulative drift in technique and practice — unclearable because undetectable without external reference.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The sense of fairness is rooted in reciprocity: those who share deserve sharing; cheaters deserve exclusion. Right and wrong are defined by social response — approval, imitation, and inclusion versus disapproval, avoidance, and exclusion. Justice is personal and immediate, not abstract. The moral foundation is the anticipation of how others will respond.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No formal law exists. Taboo and custom are transmitted by demonstration of consequences — avoidance of certain foods, places, or actions because others visibly avoid them. Regulation is informal social pressure. The code is unwritten because writing does not exist, unspoken because speech is not the primary medium. Evolution occurs through drift in practice, not deliberate reform.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are settled through confrontation, mediation by respected individuals, or avoidance. Liability is assessed in the moment by participants and observers. Sanction ranges from social disapproval to exclusion to violent retaliation. There is no formal procedure; resolution depends on the parties involved and their relative standing. The caseload is small enough for ad hoc handling.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is bounded by group dependence — one may do as one wishes if one can survive the consequences. Protection comes from kin and allies, not abstract rights. The compliance burden is the attention required to navigate social expectations learned through observation. The rules are unwritten but pervasive, enforced by the omnipresence of watching others.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Those with strong kin networks or physical dominance may escape sanction for wrongdoing. Unredressed grievance festers until discharged through later retaliation, reconciliation, or departure. The gap between justice owed and delivered is personal and situational. The residue is the standing grudge — absorbed into the relationship, resolved through violence, or carried to death.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no formal inquiry or explicit theory. Understanding of the natural world is practical and immediate: which plants are edible, where water can be found, how animals behave, what stone knaps well. The implicit paradigm is the accumulated practical knowledge of generations, transmitted by demonstration. The discovery frontier is the next successful technique variation that gets copied.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: The Levallois prepared-core technique represents sophisticated applied knowledge. The knapper envisions the desired flake and executes a planned sequence of removals to produce it. This mental template and motor sequence are learnable through imitation, representing a cognitive advance over earlier technologies. Hafting of stone points to wooden shafts compounds the technique. Engineering without words, blueprints held in practiced hands.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship through observation and copying. The knowledge stock is whatever the current generation carries in their heads. Skill distribution follows willingness and capacity to imitate. No literacy exists. The stock grows slowly as technique refines through trial and selection; much is lost when skilled practitioners die without successful imitators. Distribution is uneven — some individuals master what others cannot.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Earlier techniques persist where they remain functional; better methods supplant them through preferential imitation. Knowledge decay occurs when transmission fails — a skilled elder dies without having been successfully copied. Error accumulates when drift goes uncorrected. The residue is lost technique and degraded practice, uncleared because external reference is impossible. What was known is gone when the knower dies.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Without symbolic language, elaborated mythos cannot exist or transmit. Yet bodily tradition creates a form of identity — "we do it this way." Memory is personal and demonstrated; ancestral practice persists through continuous imitation. The foundation is embodied tradition, not narrative. Who a people are is what they do, not what they say about themselves.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No narrative or ideology exists without symbolic communication. The existing order is legitimated by its existence — this is how things are done because this is how they have been seen done. Justification is unnecessary where alternatives are inconceivable. The legitimating story is simply the absence of any other story.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture consists of stone tools, wooden implements (largely unpreserved), and possibly personal ornament. The Middle Stone Age toolkit shows regional variation, suggesting local traditions transmitted through imitation. Ochre use at some sites may indicate early symbolic behavior or may serve practical functions (hide-processing, sun protection). Artistic expression in the full sense awaits symbolic capacity; material expression is functional with possible aesthetic attention to symmetry and form.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: The Levallois tradition is productive and refining through the window, not exhausted. Regional variants suggest living traditions adapting to local conditions. Form exhaustion requires forms stable enough to stale; at this stage, continuous drift prevents crystallization. The residue is whatever techniques are abandoned — not mourned but simply not copied, their loss unregistered.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: Without symbolic language, elaborated cosmology cannot develop. The existential outlook is immediate — survival, reproduction, the cycles of day and season. Death is observed; whether it carries metaphysical meaning is unknowable. The human place in reality is unnarrated, simply lived. If there is wonder or dread at existence, it cannot be articulated or transmitted as such.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: If ritual exists, it is enacted bodily — repeated actions at certain times or places. Mortuary behavior may be emerging; treatment of the dead with apparent care appears at some contemporary sites. Whether this constitutes sacred practice or simply bodily disposal is debated. Devotion in the full sense requires concepts that may not yet exist. The sacred, if present, is demonstrated rather than explained.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No institutions or doctrine exist. There are no specialists in the sacred, no orthodoxy, no hierarchies of spiritual authority. Whatever spiritual intuitions exist are personal or transmitted through shared practice. Nothing can be taught that cannot be shown.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Without articulated belief systems, spiritual diffusion operates only at the level of practice. When populations meet and practices spread through imitation, something like syncretism may occur. But in the absence of doctrine, there is nothing to displace or blend. The phenomenon may not yet meaningfully exist.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment presumes prior enchantment that erodes. If these populations experience anything as sacred, we cannot know its vitality or decline. The residue question cannot be answered. What remains is the archaeological trace of populations who spread across the Maghreb, carrying Middle Stone Age technology and whatever else lived in their heads — all of it passed hand to hand, none of it surviving except what was successfully copied by the next pair of watching eyes.

docs.title: 1,800,000 BCE – 1,500,000 BCE — Oldowan Presence at Ain Hanech
docs.text: Summary: The earliest stone-tool makers in North Africa arrive at Ain Hanech in the Algerian Tell around 1.8 million years ago, carrying a simple but effective Oldowan toolkit of cores and flakes from sub-Saharan origins; the single most causal factor is the Saharan corridor that opened during a humid climatic phase, permitting hominin dispersal northward from East Africa into the Maghreb.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: Ain Hanech lies in the Algerian Tell, a zone of folded ridges and interior basins south of the Mediterranean coast, where seasonal watercourses cut through sedimentary deposits rich in workable cobbles; the site sits near paleolake margins that concentrated water, game, and raw material in a single accessible locale, reducing the friction of subsistence movement.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The early Pleistocene Maghreb oscillates between humid and arid phases; a humid interval opens the Saharan corridor, transforming the desert into grassland with lakes and rivers, permitting northward hominin dispersal from East Africa and sustaining occupation at Ain Hanech.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Acute hazards are minimal during humid phases; the primary risk is climatic reversal to aridity, which would close the Saharan corridor and isolate any northern population from the sub-Saharan source zone.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Local stream gravels provide abundant limestone and flint cobbles suitable for Oldowan knapping; the endowment is effectively unlimited relative to the small hominin population, with no evidence of raw-material constraint.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Knapping debris and organic refuse are trivial against the absorptive capacity of the landscape; no saturation or feedback is detectable at this population scale.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic African parasites and waterborne pathogens impose a background mortality load, but no epidemic pulse is recorded; death rates are governed primarily by predation and injury rather than disease.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Access to lakeside fauna and plant resources supports adequate caloric intake; skeletal proxies from contemporary African sites suggest robust stature and no acute nutritional stress.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Care is limited to immediate wound-tending and group support; there is no specialized healing apparatus, only the innate recovery capacity of the body and the ad hoc assistance of band members.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Hominin reproductive biology follows the slow-maturing, low-fertility pattern of the genus Homo; pairing dynamics are unknown but likely involve small multi-male, multi-female groups with opportunistic mating.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population is sparse, numbering at most a few dozen individuals in the Ain Hanech area at any time; replacement barely exceeds attrition, and the presence may represent episodic occupation rather than continuous settlement.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: High infant mortality and short adult lifespans limit the dependency load; few individuals survive to old age, and the group carries little standing burden of infirmity.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Provisioning rests on opportunistic foraging and scavenging, with stone tools enabling access to carcass meat and marrow; the subsistence floor is thin but viable in the humid-phase environment.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy capture is limited to human muscle and passive solar warmth; fire use at this date is unattested in the Maghreb, leaving the per-capita work ceiling low.

Labor Organization & Coercion: There is no formalized labor division; all able members forage, and cooperation is voluntary and situational, structured by kinship and immediate need rather than coercion.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Oldowan production is expedient, generating tools for immediate use with no surplus storage; each knapping episode produces a flake set consumed on the spot or abandoned after use.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No storage technology exists; the group carries no reserves and buffers against shortage only through mobility and the social obligation to share windfalls.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is limited to immediate sharing within the band; there is no evidence of inter-group trade or long-distance raw-material transport at Ain Hanech.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: Value cannot be stored or deferred; all provisioning is present-tense, and reciprocity operates on a short cycle of share-now, owe-later within the co-present group.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: There is no extraction apparatus; any surplus is communally consumed or abandoned, with no mechanism for accumulation or reallocation.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Wealth does not exist as a category; tools are made and discarded, and no individual holds durable property worth defending.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Knapping debris and butchery waste are left at the site; the volume is trivial and absorbed without routing decision or consequence.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship likely structures the band, with maternal bonds forming the stable core; inheritance is meaningless absent durable property, and group membership follows from birth and proximity.

Association & Mutual Aid: Mutual aid is embedded in band life; sharing of food and assistance in foraging are obligatory, and no separate associational fabric exists beyond the kinship group.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in grooming, rest, and the imitative play through which young learn knapping and foraging by watching and copying adults.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Stratification is minimal; status differences may exist by age and sex, but there is no formalized hierarchy, and leadership is situational rather than permanent.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; the band is self-organizing, and decision-making is ad hoc, based on immediate circumstance and the influence of experienced individuals.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: There is no organized coercive capacity; violence is interpersonal and situational, and the group lacks any monopoly on force or means of collective enforcement.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is low given small group size; disputes are resolved through avoidance or immediate confrontation, and no unmetabolized grievance accumulates at scale.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal, exercised by individuals who demonstrate competence in foraging or knapping; authority is personal and context-dependent, not institutionalized.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to the band as a survival unit; there is no abstract order to legitimate, and belonging is felt rather than argued.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective will is episodic, coalescing around immediate challenges such as predator defense or group movement; there is no sustained political project or contest for power.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands, if any are encountered, are unknown; the population is so sparse that inter-group contact may be rare, and posture is likely cautious and avoidant.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The prevailing mood is immediate and situational; trust extends to known band members, and the behavioral temper is shaped by the daily cycle of foraging, rest, and social interaction.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection is not legible at this scale; the affective life is immediate, and exhaustion or estrangement would manifest as individual departure rather than collective malaise.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is gestural and vocal but pre-linguistic; meaning is conveyed through pointing, demonstration, and vocalization, with mutual intelligibility limited to the co-present group.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of direct observation; there is no channel extending beyond line of sight and earshot, and transmission velocity is bounded by physical proximity.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No record exists; knowledge persists only in living memory, and each generation must relearn techniques by watching and copying those who carry them.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: There is no framing apparatus or censorship; what can be communicated is limited only by the expressive capacity of gesture and the recipient's ability to interpret it.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is face-to-face; there is no amplification, and information propagates only through direct demonstration within the band.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is high in direct transmission but degrades with each retransmission; the imitative mode introduces drift, and knowledge simplifies or distorts across generations.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The moral sense is proto-ethical, grounded in the immediate expectations of sharing and reciprocity within the band; fairness is felt rather than codified.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: There is no law; conduct is regulated by expectation and consequence, not by rule, and no codification exists.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved immediately through confrontation or avoidance; there is no adjudicating body, and sanction is personal and retaliatory rather than systematic.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Rights do not exist as a category; individuals are protected by band membership and kinship obligation, not by rule, and there is no compliance burden.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed immediately or not at all; there is no standing deficit of justice, only the immediate dynamics of retaliation and reconciliation.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no formal inquiry; understanding is practical and embedded in action, with no separation between knowing and doing.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Oldowan knapping is the technical method, passed by imitation: selecting a cobble, striking at the correct angle to detach a flake, recognizing a usable edge; the technique is simple but effective and requires sustained observation to learn.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is entirely imitative; young learn by watching adults, hand guiding hand, and the knowledge stock is what living practitioners can demonstrate; skill distribution is relatively even across adults.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays with each practitioner who dies without transmitting; the imitative mode is fragile, and skill can be lost within a generation if transmission fails.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no mythos or narrative memory; identity is immediate, rooted in the band and the landscape, with no story of origins or collective past.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists; the order needs no justification because there is no alternative to imagine against it.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is purely functional; Oldowan tools show no decorative elaboration, and the aesthetic dimension is absent or undetectable.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: There is no cultural form to exhaust; meaning is immediate and instrumental, and no symbolic residue accumulates.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: There is no detectable cosmology; the hominin mind at this stage may not yet frame existential questions, and the sacred is not a legible category.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual is attested; behavior is instrumental, and devotional practice, if any, leaves no trace.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists; there is no clergy, no doctrine, no authority over the sacred.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: There is no spiritual system to diffuse or displace; the category does not apply.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment presupposes enchantment; here the sacred has not yet emerged, and there is no residue of lost transcendence.

docs.title: 315,000 BCE – 280,000 BCE — The Jebel Irhoud Population and Early Homo sapiens
docs.text: Summary: A population of early Homo sapiens occupied a baryte mining site in the Moroccan interior during a humid climatic window, producing Middle Stone Age lithics with Levallois technique. The binding constraint is the imitative stage itself: modern facial anatomy appears here alongside archaic braincase morphology, yet everything known persists only in living heads and passes hand to hand. This event marks a turning point in human biological history — the earliest dated appearance of our species — while the mode of cultural transmission remains unchanged from earlier hominin populations, still wholly dependent on direct demonstration and copying without speech or symbol.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: Jebel Irhoud sits roughly 100 kilometers inland from the Atlantic coast, in the foothills west of the High Atlas. The site occupies a karstic cave system formed in baryte-bearing limestone, opening onto an interior plateau dissected by seasonal watercourses. Access from the coast requires traversing rolling terrain; the Atlas chain presents a steeper barrier to southern movement, while the interior plateau permits relatively unimpeded east-west travel.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The occupation falls within Marine Isotope Stage 9-7, a humid interglacial phase bringing increased rainfall, expanded vegetation, and perennial water sources to the Moroccan interior. Atlantic-derived moisture penetrates inland; the northern Sahara contracts, opening biological corridors southward. Temperature regimes are warm-temperate, with reduced seasonality compared to glacial phases. This Green Sahara window enables occupation of sites otherwise marginal.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Seismic activity from Atlas tectonics poses occasional ground-shaking risk; cave collapse from structural failure of karstic chambers represents the primary acute hazard. Flash flooding of seasonal watercourses during intense rainfall events threatens low-lying camps. Fire, whether natural or anthropogenic, periodically sweeps the surrounding scrubland. Margin against these hazards is the mobility of small populations able to relocate.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The baryte outcrop provides the raw material that will later attract commercial mining. More immediately relevant, flint and quartzite nodules suitable for knapping are locally available. Water sources, while seasonal, are adequate during humid phases. Fauna includes gazelle, zebra, wildebeest, and hartebeest — a grazing community indicating open grassland with scattered woodland. Edible plants expand during humid windows.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Population densities are low enough that organic waste disperses and decomposes without accumulation. Lithic debitage accumulates at knapping stations but imposes no ecological load. No evidence of sink saturation; the landscape absorbs all anthropogenic discharge without degradation. The residue is nil — cleared by natural processes faster than it accretes.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic parasites and zoonotic diseases circulate at background levels consistent with African savanna environments. Mortality from infection is episodic rather than constant. Wound infection following injury, intestinal parasites, and occasional epidemic die-offs from novel pathogens likely elevate baseline mortality above modern standards. The direction is stable within the humid window; no epidemic spike is evidenced.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The Jebel Irhoud skeletal remains indicate robust, well-nourished individuals. Stature and limb proportions fall within the range of early Homo sapiens from other African sites. Dental wear patterns suggest a mixed diet of meat and fibrous plant material. The humid climate supports adequate provisioning; there are no signs of chronic nutritional stress in the available specimens.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity rests entirely on the bodies' own regenerative powers and whatever wound-tending behaviors the group practices — cleaning, immobilization, herbal application — transmitted by imitation. One individual shows healed trauma, indicating survival of injury with group support. The capacity is limited to what can be demonstrated and copied; no systematic medicine exists.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: The population displays modern sapiens reproductive biology: extended juvenile dependency, high parental investment, and flexible pair-bonding. The remains represent multiple individuals of varying ages, suggesting a multi-generational group with active reproduction. Selective pressures favor cognitive development and social cooperation.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is very low — likely fewer than one person per hundred square kilometers averaged across the habitable zone. The Jebel Irhoud sample represents perhaps 20-30 individuals accumulated over the occupation span, suggesting small band sizes of 15-30 living at any time. Replacement is marginal; population growth is near zero or slightly positive during favorable climatic phases.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Extended childhood dependency characterizes the species. Elderly individuals, where they survive, become repositories of imitative knowledge but also consumers of provisioning. The productive cohort absorbs this load without apparent strain in the evidence, but the ratio of dependents to providers is structurally elevated compared to earlier hominins with shorter juvenile periods. The residue is the biological cost of extended learning — cleared by the cohort if surplus permits, accumulating as abandonment if it does not.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Hunting and gathering provide all subsistence. Gazelle and other grazing ungulates are hunted, likely by ambush or persistence techniques demonstrated through imitation. Plant foods — roots, tubers, seeds, fruits — are gathered seasonally. Provisioning sits comfortably above starvation during humid phases; the carrying-capacity edge is distant while rainfall supports game and vegetation.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Fire is controlled and used for cooking, warmth, and possibly landscape management. Human muscle provides all work for toolmaking, hunting, processing, and transport. No animal or mechanical power is harnessed. Per-capita energy throughput is low but adequate for survival and reproduction. The efficiency ceiling is set by human physiology and the limits of imitative technique transfer.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor is organized by task and circumstance, not by formalized division. All capable adults participate in provisioning; specialization is minimal and ad hoc. There is no coercion beyond social pressure transmitted through demonstration and response. Children learn by watching and helping; instruction is entirely imitative.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production consists of lithic tool manufacture, food acquisition, and camp maintenance. The Middle Stone Age toolkit at Jebel Irhoud includes Levallois prepared-core technology, indicating increased cognitive planning and skill transmission. Surplus above immediate consumption is minimal and ephemeral — a successful hunt provides temporary abundance quickly consumed or lost to spoilage.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No durable storage exists. Reserves are the bodies of living individuals who can temporarily carry fat, and the landscape itself which buffers against local scarcity through mobility. A failed hunt or dry spell is absorbed by moving to better-provisioned territory or reducing activity. Risk-pooling is social — sharing within the band — but no material buffer accumulates.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is immediate and reciprocal within the band; delayed reciprocity extends only as far as individual memory can track. No evidence of inter-group trade networks; raw material procurement is local. Logistics consists of walking while carrying what can be held. The home range spans perhaps tens of kilometers centered on water sources.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No unit of account or durable value-store exists. Obligation is personal and remembered, tracking who shared and who received. Credit is implicit in the expectation that today's sharing will be reciprocated when fortune reverses. This deferred reciprocity is the only form of value-transfer across time, and it cannot be inscribed or externalized — it lives only in heads.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Redistribution is immediate sharing: a successful hunter distributes meat to kin and allies by demonstration of social norm rather than extraction. No formal tribute or taxation exists. The surplus flow is from the lucky to the unlucky within the band, not from producers to a ruling stratum.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Material possessions are portable tools and gathered resources, held individually but shared readily. No durable wealth accumulates; concentration is impossible when nothing survives longer than its holder. Defense consists of carrying one's tools and not leaving them. The residue is simply the broken and discarded — lithic debitage and bone fragments — abandoned at camp.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste is left at camps and scavenged by other animals or decomposed. Lithic waste — cores, flakes, debitage — is left in place, forming the archaeological record. Neither type accumulates as a problem; the waste stream is absorbed by the environment without requiring management. The residue is archaeologically productive and ecologically negligible.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship organizes the band. Nuclear families embedded within extended kin networks form the basic unit. Inheritance is biological — offspring inherit nothing but what they can learn by watching elders. Marriage or pair-bonding patterns are unknown but likely flexible, with recognition of biological relatedness and incest avoidance.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the primary association, likely numbering 15-30 individuals at Jebel Irhoud. Mutual aid is obligatory within kin; reciprocity extends to all band members. Cooperation in hunting, childcare, and camp defense structures daily life. There are no guilds or formal organizations — only the informal mutual reliance of co-resident kin.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in sociability, grooming, play, and rest. Children play at adult activities, learning through imitation. Shared meals are social occasions. No evidence of games or sports, but the primate heritage suggests play continues into adulthood. Social bonding through proximity and shared activity maintains group cohesion.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status is informal, based on demonstrated competence, age, and perhaps physical prowess or hunting success. No formal hierarchy exists beyond the deference accorded to experienced adults. Factional divisions, where they exist, would follow kinship lines. Boundaries between groups are permeable; individuals may transfer between bands through mating or fission events.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists. Decisions are made by consensus or deference to experienced individuals. There are no offices, bureaucracies, or formal procedures. Record-keeping is impossible without external memory; coordination is face-to-face and immediate. Capacity is limited to what can be accomplished by direct communication within the band.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: No organized coercive capacity exists. Violence, where it occurs, is individual or small-group — conflict over mates, resources, or status. Weaponry consists of hunting tools — pointed stones, wooden spears — which double as weapons. No fortification or formal military organization. Balance of force is rough equality among adult males; no party can compel others systematically.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is discharged through fission — individuals or families leaving to join other bands when conflict becomes intolerable. Grievance is personal and resolved by avoidance, reconciliation, or departure. Crime, vendetta, and rebellion as concepts do not apply to a scale where everyone knows everyone. The residue is the occasional violent death and the chronic low-level friction of intimate community — absorbed or triggering departure.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational and personal. An experienced hunter leads the hunt; a knowledgeable elder guides camp placement. Authority derives from demonstrated competence, not formal office. Charisma — the ability to draw others' attention and imitation — matters for influence. No permanent leaders exist; authority shifts with task and circumstance.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to kin and band, not to abstract authority. The "right to command" does not exist as a concept; compliance follows from trust in demonstrated competence. Disaffection manifests as departure, not rebellion. Legitimacy is personal and constantly renegotiated through interaction.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action requires assembling individual wills in the moment — the decision to hunt, to move, to confront a threat. There is no standing political will or institutional resolve. Mobilization is ad hoc, driven by immediate need and led by whoever steps forward. The struggle for power is the competition for attention and imitation.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands are unknown but likely range from wary avoidance to peaceful exchange of mates, depending on kinship ties and resource competition. Expansion is simply moving into unoccupied territory during favorable conditions. Deterrence is the demonstrated capacity for violence. No formal diplomacy or sustained antagonism exists.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The emotional life of the Jebel Irhoud population is unrecoverable, but the framework of small-group living suggests high interpersonal familiarity, frequent face-to-face interaction, and trust calibrated by repeated encounters. Anxiety focuses on immediate threats — predators, hunger, injury. Confidence rises with successful hunts and favorable weather. The behavioral temper is cautious, alert, and socially attentive.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Exhaustion from failed hunts, injury, or interpersonal conflict can drain will. Chronic failure may lead to apathy, social withdrawal, or departure. The discharge mechanism is fission — the disaffected leave rather than accumulate as a resentful core. The residue is whatever grief, distrust, or exhaustion persists in individuals unable to act — absorbed through time or carried to the grave.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: The binding constraint of the imitative stage: communication occurs through gesture, demonstration, vocalization, facial expression, and bodily imitation, but not through language as a fully symbolic system. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band but may fail across populations separated by time and space. Meaning is transmitted by showing, not telling. The code is embodied, not abstract.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of physical proximity — voice-range or line-of-sight. No channel extends beyond immediate presence. Transmission to distant individuals requires physical travel. News does not precede its carrier. The reach is the band; beyond that, information stops.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists. Memory is living memory only — held in heads, passed by demonstration. When a knowledgeable individual dies, their knowledge dies with them unless it has been imitated by another. Drift is inevitable with each transmission; fidelity depends on the copier's attention and ability. The archaeological record preserves material culture but not the knowledge used to make it.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Without symbolic language, framing in the modern sense does not apply. Social norms govern who may approach, touch, or imitate whom — the young imitate the old, the novice the expert. Taboo may exist around certain actions or objects, transmitted by aversive response rather than verbal prohibition. The permitted band is whatever can be demonstrated and accepted.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is the scarce resource. Information propagates when it captures attention and is successfully copied. Amplification consists of repeated demonstration. Virality is the rapid spread of a useful technique through imitation. Reception depends on proximity, relationship, and the imitator's capacity.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Every transmission introduces drift — the copier's variation on what was demonstrated. There is no mechanism for verification against an original; no original persists. Signal integrity depends on redundancy — multiple demonstrations, multiple copiers. Noise accumulates across generations. The residue is the cumulative drift in technique and knowledge, uncleared because unclearable.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The sense of fairness is visceral, rooted in reciprocity — those who share deserve sharing, cheaters deserve exclusion. Right and wrong are defined by social response: approval and imitation versus disapproval and avoidance. Justice is immediate and personal, not abstract. Conscience is the anticipation of others' reactions.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No formal law exists and none can exist without external memory. Taboo and custom are transmitted by demonstration of aversive response — avoiding certain foods, places, or actions because others visibly avoid them. Regulation is the informal pressure of social attention. The code is unwritten because writing does not exist; it is unspoken because speech is not yet the primary medium.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are settled by confrontation, mediation by respected individuals, or avoidance. Liability is assessed in the moment by participants and witnesses. Sanction ranges from shunning to violent retaliation. There is no formal procedure; resolution depends on the parties and their relative standing. Judgment keeps pace with the caseload because both are small.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is high within the constraints of group dependence — one may do as one wishes if one can survive the social response. Protection comes from kin and allies, not from abstract rights. The compliance burden is simply the attention required to navigate social expectations learned by watching others.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Those with strong kin networks or physical dominance may escape sanction for wrongs. Unredressed grievance festers until discharged through later retaliation or departure. The gap between justice owed and delivered is personal and situational. The residue is the standing grudge — absorbed into the relationship or carried until death.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
