Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral intuitions are pre-codified — fairness in sharing, resentment at free-riding, protectiveness toward kin and the young. Justice is immediate and emotional, not reasoned.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No laws or codified rules. Conduct is regulated by habit, imitation, and social sanction.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved by dominance, avoidance, or fission. There is no formal adjudication; sanction is social exclusion or physical confrontation.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No concept of rights; individuals have what they can hold. Compliance burden is minimal — conform to group norms or leave.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed immediately or not at all. No accumulation of unredressed grievance beyond individual memory.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry or theory. Understanding is practical and embedded in action — knowing how, not knowing that.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical knowledge includes stone-flaking (minimal evidence in Java), carcass processing, plant identification, fire use (if present), and wayfinding. All transmitted by demonstration.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship by observation. The knowledge stock is limited to what living individuals carry. Skill distribution depends on individual aptitude and exposure.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays with death. A technique lost is lost permanently unless reinvented. Transmission drift degrades fidelity over generations.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: No mythos or narrative memory exists. Identity is immediate — membership in this band, recognition of these faces. There is no sense of a collective past or future.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative; the order is self-evident because it is all that is known.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is expedient tools and processed carcasses. No ornamentation, no symbolic marking, no deliberate aesthetic. Objects are made for use and discarded.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: There are no symbolic forms to exhaust. The repertoire is stable because minimal.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No articulated cosmology. The world is immediate and present; there is no evidence of abstract thought about origins or endings.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual practice is attested. Repeated behaviors exist but lack the symbolic elaboration that defines ritual.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institutions or doctrine.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: No spiritual beliefs to spread or displace.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: No sacred realm exists to become disenchanted. The world is unsacralized, neither enchanted nor disenchanted.

docs.title: 1,400,000 BCE – 1,000,000 BCE — Early Sangiran Population and Trinil Fauna
docs.text: Summary: Homo erectus is now established at Sangiran, the population growing slowly within a rich Jetis-fauna environment of megaherbivores, large bovids, and open woodland. The central constraint is the carrying capacity set by tropical foraging returns — the population remains sparse, dispersed, and tightly bound to faunal abundance, with no mechanism to buffer against local depletion or environmental shift.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Solo Basin remains the core habitat, with Sangiran's sedimentary domes preserving the densest fossil record. The Bengawan Solo and its tributaries provide water and movement corridors through mixed woodland and open grassland. The volcanic uplands to the south supply ash and lahar deposits that periodically bury and preserve surfaces. Movement within the basin is easy; the landscape is open enough for large-mammal tracking.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The climate is tropical monsoonal, warm year-round with a marked wet-dry seasonality. Interglacial conditions prevail for much of this interval, maintaining forest-savanna mosaic. Glacial cycles continue to modulate sea level, but Java remains connected to the Sunda shelf during low-stands, permitting faunal exchange with the mainland.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Volcanic activity continues along the central Javanese arc. Ash falls, lahars, and pyroclastic events are periodic hazards, though they also fertilize soils and create fossil-preserving deposits. Flooding along the Solo drainage poses seasonal risk but also concentrates carcasses for scavenging.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The Jetis fauna — the older faunal assemblage predating the classic Trinil fauna — includes Stegodon, Hexaprotodon (hippopotamus), large bovids, suids, cervids, and carnivores including tigers and hyenas. Plant resources are abundant: fruiting trees, tubers, and bamboo. Water is reliable.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Population density remains negligible; the environment absorbs all hominin impact without measurable effect. Bone refuse accumulates at processing sites but is scattered and rapidly decomposed or buried.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Tropical disease burden continues — intestinal parasites, vector-borne fevers, bacterial infections. Mortality is high by modern standards but stable; the population persists, indicating adaptation to local pathogens. Large carnivores remain a predation risk.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Sangiran crania and post-cranial fragments show robust, well-nourished individuals with heavy muscle markings and thick cortical bone. Cranial capacity averages 800–900 cc, within the lower Homo erectus range. Dental wear indicates coarse, gritty diets requiring heavy mastication.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing remains limited to rest, wound-tending, and group tolerance. Some Sangiran specimens show healed fractures, indicating survival of significant injuries — evidence of care or at least non-abandonment of the injured.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Reproductive patterns remain typical of Homo erectus: extended juvenile dependency, likely pair-bonding or serial monogamy, and high infant mortality offset by continued reproduction through the fertile years. The population is now large enough to avoid immediate inbreeding depression.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density remains low — perhaps a few hundred individuals across the Solo Basin and surrounding areas. Growth is slow; the population replaces itself but does not expand rapidly. Age structure is heavily weighted toward reproductively active adults.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Few individuals survive to old age; the dependent load is minimal. Most adults remain productive until death from disease, accident, or predation.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Subsistence is foraging with an emphasis on large-mammal exploitation — hunting and scavenging Stegodon, bovids, and cervids supplemented by plant foods. The megafauna provide high caloric returns per acquisition event. Provisioning is immediate-return; no storage.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy capture is human muscle, supplemented by fire where used for cooking and defense. Evidence for controlled fire in Java at this date is ambiguous but plausible. The work ceiling is set by human physiology.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor is cooperative and task-specific: group drives or ambush hunting for large game, shared processing of carcasses, collective plant gathering. Division follows age and sex. No coercion beyond informal social pressure.

Production & Surplus Capacity: No surplus production. Large kills may temporarily exceed immediate consumption but spoil without preservation. Any excess is shared and consumed within the band over days.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No material storage. Buffering is biological — body fat, group sharing — and behavioral — mobility to new foraging patches when local returns decline.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is intra-band sharing. No evidence of inter-group trade or exchange networks. Logistics is movement of the band to resources, not movement of resources to the band.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No value storage. Reciprocity is immediate and face-to-face; there is no deferred obligation beyond memory of past sharing.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: No extraction apparatus. Distribution follows informal sharing norms — successful hunters distribute to kin and band members without formal obligation.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: No wealth accumulation. All individuals are materially equivalent. Possessions are tools and perhaps infant carriers; nothing is defended as property.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Bone and plant waste accumulate at processing and habitation sites. No deliberate routing; natural decomposition and burial by sediment clear residues over time.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship structures remain simple multi-generational bands with mother-offspring bonds as the stable core. Pair-bonds may exist but are not institutionalized. Inheritance is meaningless absent heritable property.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the unit of cooperation. Mutual aid is obligatory: shared food, collective childcare, group defense against predators. Cooperation is maintained by kinship, familiarity, and reciprocity.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-foraging time is spent in rest, grooming, and social interaction. Juvenile play reinforces motor skills and social bonds. Adults engage in low-intensity sociability during rest periods.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Stratification is minimal. Status differences may exist based on age, hunting success, or physical dominance, but these are fluid and situational. No permanent hierarchy; egalitarianism is enforced by the ease of fission.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administration or institutions. Coordination is achieved through imitation, gesture, and direct observation. Group decisions emerge from consensus or follow experienced individuals.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: No organized coercion. Violence is occasional and interpersonal — over mates, food shares, or dominance. Weapons are opportunistic tools. Defense against predators is collective.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social tension is discharged through spatial fission — disgruntled individuals leave. No accumulated grievance or structural decay; the organization is too simple to ossify.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal and context-dependent. Experienced hunters lead during hunts; knowledgeable individuals guide foraging routes. Authority dissolves when the task ends.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is personal and kin-based. There is no abstract order to legitimate; individuals follow those they know through direct relationship.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is coordinated but not deliberated. The band acts together by habit and necessity. There is no political sphere distinct from daily cooperation.

External Relations & Posture: Other bands are rarely encountered. When contact occurs, it is likely cautious — potential mates, potential competitors, potential threats. No sustained inter-group relations.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The prevailing temper is practical — focused on daily subsistence with emotional responses tied to immediate circumstances. Trust is high within the band, cautious toward strangers. Fear of predators is constant; satisfaction follows successful hunts.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection does not accumulate; the option of departure prevents festering grievance. Apathy is incompatible with the demands of foraging life.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication remains gestural, postural, and vocal but pre-linguistic. Complex information is conveyed through demonstration and imitation. Vocalization conveys emotional state and alarm. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of individuals. There is no communication at distance; all transmission is face-to-face. Range is limited to immediate proximity.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record. All knowledge exists in living memory. The death of an experienced individual erases their accumulated knowledge unless previously demonstrated to others.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: No framing apparatus. Communication is direct, situational, and transparent within the limits of pre-linguistic expression. No censorship or deliberate concealment.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by movement, sound, and urgency. No amplification; influence is limited to direct presence.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Transmission drift is inherent in imitative learning. Each demonstration introduces variation; there is no mechanism to standardize or correct. Skills and knowledge degrade without reinforcement.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral intuitions are embedded in practice — fairness in meat-sharing, protection of young, resentment of cheaters. Justice is emotional and immediate, not codified or reasoned.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No laws exist. Conduct is regulated by habit, imitation, and informal sanction. Norms are implicit in behavior, not articulated as rules.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are settled by dominance, avoidance, or departure. There is no formal adjudication. Sanction is social — exclusion, reduced sharing, physical confrontation.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No concept of rights. Individuals have what they can hold and defend. Compliance is simply conformity to group practice.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed immediately or forgotten. No accumulated backlog of injustice; memory is short and departure easy.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry or theory. Knowledge is practical and embodied — knowing how to track, butcher, find water, avoid predators. Understanding is embedded in action, not abstracted into propositions.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical repertoire includes large-mammal butchery, stone-flaking (minimal in Java), plant processing, fire use (if present), and landscape navigation. All skills are transmitted by demonstration and imitation.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is observation and practice alongside experienced individuals. The knowledge stock is limited to what the living population carries. Skill distribution depends on individual aptitude and the chance of exposure to competent demonstrators.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays with death. There is no external storage to preserve superseded techniques; loss is permanent. Transmission drift erodes fidelity over generations.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: No narrative memory or mythos. Identity is immediate — recognition of band members, familiarity with home range. There is no sense of collective history or future.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative. The social order requires no justification because no alternative is conceivable.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is expedient and unadorned — stone flakes, bone fragments used as tools, perhaps wooden implements (unpreserved). No ornamentation, no symbolic marking, no deliberate aesthetic.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: No symbolic forms exist to exhaust. The material repertoire is stable because minimal and purely functional.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No articulated cosmology. The world is immediate and present. There is no evidence of reflection on origins, death, or the nature of existence.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual practice is attested. Repeated behaviors exist — daily routines, seasonal movements — but lack symbolic elaboration.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institutions or doctrine. The concept does not apply.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: No spiritual beliefs to spread or displace.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: No sacred realm exists. The world is neither enchanted nor disenchanted; the category does not apply to pre-symbolic cognition.

docs.title: 200,000 BCE – 100,000 BCE — Environmental Oscillation and Population Response
docs.text: Summary: Across one hundred millennia the Sunda Shelf undergoes repeated glacial-interglacial transitions, each swing redrawing coastlines by hundreds of kilometers and alternately uniting and fragmenting Homo erectus populations; the binding constraint is this rhythm of connection and isolation, which pulses gene flow and local adaptation without any capacity for cultural buffering beyond what bodies can demonstrate and hands can copy.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: During glacial maxima sea level drops 80–120 meters, exposing a vast lowland plain linking Java, Sumatra, and Borneo to mainland Asia; river systems extend across what are now shallow seas, and the coastline retreats hundreds of kilometers. Interglacial high stands submerge these corridors, fragmenting continuous habitat into island chains and creating the modern island configuration. Transit friction oscillates: low stands permit unimpeded terrestrial movement across Sundaland, high stands impose sea barriers that only driftwood or swimming can cross.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The region remains tropical throughout, but precipitation patterns shift with glacial state; lowland grassland-forest mosaics expand during cooler drier phases, while closed-canopy rainforest contracts to upland refugia. Interglacials restore wetter conditions and forest dominance. Temperature swings are modest by high-latitude standards but sufficient to alter plant and animal communities.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Volcanic activity along the Sunda arc persists; Krakatau and the Sumatran chain episodically blanket portions of the shelf in ash. Flooding accompanies monsoon intensification during warm phases. Drought risk rises during glacial maxima as monsoons weaken. Populations hold no engineered margin against these shocks.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Large mammal biomass tracks habitat area; low stands that expand Sundaland also expand grazing landscapes supporting Stegodon, rhinoceros, and bovids. Plant resources shift with forest cover. Freshwater availability fluctuates with river course changes as drainage reorganizes across the exposed shelf.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: At the population densities and subsistence modes of Homo erectus bands, anthropogenic waste loads are negligible; natural decomposition and fluvial dispersal clear organic refuse without saturation.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Tropical pathogen pressure remains high; malaria, intestinal parasites, and waterborne infections exact a baseline toll. The relatively low population density limits epidemic transmission but does not eliminate endemic disease. Mortality is elevated relative to temperate zones but stable across the window.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Robust skeletal remains from the Ngandong series indicate large-bodied, physically powerful adults adapted to active foraging. Nutrition tracks game availability; low stands that expand savanna likely improve protein access, while forest-dominated interglacials shift diets toward plant foods and smaller game.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Care is limited to what group members can provide through direct assistance: wound cleaning, immobilization, food sharing. No pharmacological knowledge can be stored or transmitted except through observed imitation. Recovery depends on individual constitution and the group's willingness to carry injured members.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Pair-bonding and extended juvenile dependence characterize the species; sexual maturation is slow, and interbirth intervals are long relative to body size. Mating patterns cannot be reconstructed from skeletal evidence but likely involve polygyny and male competition.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is low, perhaps a few individuals per hundred square kilometers. Band sizes are small, likely 20–50 members. Replacement is slow; high infant and juvenile mortality limits net growth. Population tracks available habitat area, expanding during low stands and contracting during high stands.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Few individuals survive to old age; the dependency load is primarily young children. The productive cohort absorbs this load through food sharing without accumulating a significant elder population.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Foraging provides the provisioning floor; there is no cultivation, no storage beyond daily carry capacity. The population lives close to the margin, with surplus rare and transient. Household pooling occurs through food sharing within the band.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle provides all motive power. Fire is present but its use for cooking, warmth, and predator deterrence is opportunistic rather than systematic. No tools amplify energy conversion beyond sharpened stone and shaped wood.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Division of labor follows age and sex without formal specialization. There is no coercion beyond dominance hierarchies; labor is mobilized by immediate need and group cohesion, not command or exchange.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is consumption; nothing is produced beyond immediate use. No surplus accumulates, and no capacity exists to store or transmit production methods except through direct observation.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: Body fat is the only buffer against shortage. There are no granaries, caches, or reserves. A failed season means reduced intake, increased mortality, and possible band dissolution.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: No trade exists. Raw materials are locally sourced; tool stone travels only as far as the band carries it. There is no exchange network linking dispersed groups.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of value exists. Reciprocity operates through immediate food sharing and remembered obligation, but memory cannot outlast the parties involved.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Dominant individuals may claim priority access to food or mates, but no institutionalized extraction occurs. Redistribution is ad hoc sharing, not systematic allocation.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: There are no durable assets to distribute or defend. Positional advantage is ephemeral, tied to individual strength and social standing.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste disperses naturally; bone and lithic debris accumulate at occupation sites but without exceeding the landscape's absorptive capacity.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship is recognized through maternal bonds and sibling familiarity; no formal marriage rules or inheritance customs can be documented. Pair bonds form and dissolve without ceremony. Property does not exist to be inherited.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole unit of association. Mutual aid is expressed through food sharing, collective defense, and cooperative hunting. No institutions exist beyond face-to-face interaction.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Play among juveniles transmits foraging and social skills through imitation. Adults engage in grooming and proximity maintenance. Festive structure, if any, is not recoverable from the archaeological record.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Dominance hierarchies exist based on physical prowess and age. Status is individual and transient, not heritable. No castes, classes, or permanent factions exist.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists. Decision-making is distributed and immediate, resolved through dominance, consensus, or fission of the band.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Coercion is individual and interpersonal. There are no specialized fighters, no weapons beyond hunting tools, and no organized violence between groups recoverable from the record.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Conflict resolves through submission, avoidance, or band fission. Grievance cannot accumulate across generations because there is no medium to transmit it. Disorder is absorbed by the flexibility of band structure.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal, situational, and based on demonstrated competence in hunting, defense, or social negotiation. No office or title exists; authority must be continually earned through action.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to the band and its dominant members, maintained through daily interaction. There is no abstract order to legitimate and no ideology to justify hierarchy.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is coordinated through imitation and response to dominant individuals. There is no deliberation, no persuasion through argument, only demonstration and following.

External Relations & Posture: Relations between bands are unknown; population density is low enough that encounters may be rare. Where bands meet, outcomes likely range from avoidance to interbreeding to conflict, resolved without lasting institutions.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Affective states are immediate and interpersonal. Trust extends to familiar band members; strangers provoke wariness. Mood tracks environmental conditions and social standing without cultural mediation.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Individual withdrawal, depression, or exhaustion occurs but does not accumulate as a social fact. The band's affective tone resets with personnel turnover and environmental change.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is gestural, postural, and possibly vocal but not linguistic. Meaning is carried by demonstration, not symbol. Mutual legibility depends on shared experience and proximity.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels no faster than a walking individual. There is no way to send a message ahead or store one for later retrieval. Knowledge is tied to bodies and present context.

Record, Storage & Persistence: There is no record. Memory is individual and dies with the carrier. Collective knowledge persists only through overlapping generations of imitation.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: There is no discourse to frame or censor. Communication is situational and immediate, not propositional.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by movement, sound, and social cues. There is no mechanism for amplification beyond the reach of voice and gesture.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal decay is rapid; any technique not continually demonstrated risks loss. The noise floor is the limit of imitative fidelity across generations.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral intuitions exist — fairness in food sharing, outrage at cheating — but cannot be articulated or codified. Justice is enacted through immediate response, not rule application.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: There is no law, no code, no rule that can be stated or stored. Conduct is regulated by dominance, habit, and immediate sanction.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved by force, submission, or avoidance. There is no third-party adjudication, no formal liability, no graduated sanction beyond individual retaliation.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No rights exist as claims on others. Protection comes from the band's collective interest in each member's contribution. Compliance is to immediate social pressure, not abstract obligation.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed or forgotten within the lifespan of the parties. There is no accumulated backlog of injustice because there is no record to maintain it.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no inquiry, no theory, no paradigm. Understanding is practical and immediate: which plants are edible, which animals can be taken, which places are dangerous. Knowledge is know-how, not know-that.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Tool-making persists through imitation; the Oldowan/Mode 1 tradition continues with little elaboration. Bone and bamboo may serve as tools but leave minimal archaeological trace. The technical repertoire is stable across the entire window.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Skills are transmitted by observation and practice. There is no teaching in the sense of intentional pedagogy; learning occurs through participation. The knowledge stock is the sum of living practitioners' competencies.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Techniques are lost when their practitioners die without successors. The sparse lithic record on Java may reflect repeated loss and reinvention as much as reliance on organic materials.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no mythos, no narrative identity, no origin story. Identity is immediate: this band, these individuals, this place. Memory is episodic and does not aggregate into collective history.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No order exists that requires legitimation. Dominance is self-evident; it needs no story to justify it.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: No unambiguous art survives from this window. Material culture is utilitarian: tools, food refuse, fire-cracked rock. If symbolic behavior exists, it leaves no durable trace.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: There are no forms to exhaust, no symbols to hollow out. The cultural dimension is minimal — the floor beneath which nothing lies.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No cosmology can be attributed. The existential outlook is immediate: present danger, present need, present satisfaction. There is no recoverable evidence of metaphysical concern.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual is attested. If repeated actions serve social bonding, they do not leave archaeological signatures distinguishable from practical activity.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: There are no institutions, no doctrine, no authority. The spiritual dimension is empty or unrecoverable.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: There is nothing to diffuse, blend, or displace. If beliefs exist, they are local, transient, and invisible to the archaeological record.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: The concept does not apply. There is no enchantment to lose, no sacred frame to erode. The spiritual register is silent.

docs.title: 1,000,000 BCE – 700,000 BCE — Homo erectus Establishment on Java
docs.text: Summary: A snapshot of Homo erectus populations consolidated in the Sangiran dome of central Java during a 300,000-year window when the species had moved past initial colonization into stable, multi-generational occupation. The binding constraint is the imitative transfer of survival skills across generations without language: every technique for procuring food, avoiding predators, and navigating the volcanic landscape must be demonstrated in person and copied by watching hands, limiting the complexity and geographic reach of any behavioral repertoire.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Sangiran dome in central Java presents a dissected volcanic landscape with braided river systems draining from Quaternary volcanoes. Fluvial deposits in the Sangiran Formation preserve the hominin record in layered silts and sands. The terrain is traversable but compartmentalized by river valleys, creating local foraging territories bounded by natural corridors. The surrounding Solo Basin provides open savanna-woodland mosaic intersected by gallery forest along watercourses. Wallace's Line lies to the east, marking a biogeographic boundary the erectus population never crossed except via rare waif dispersal.

Climate Regime & Volatility: Tropical equatorial conditions prevail, with monsoon-driven wet and dry seasons. Temperatures remain warm year-round. Glacial-interglacial oscillations affect sea level rather than local temperature; during glacial lowstands the Java Sea floor is exposed as savanna, connecting Java to the Sunda mainland. The climate is stable within any human lifetime but drifts across the window, with cooler, drier phases favoring open habitats.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Volcanic activity from the Kendeng and other Quaternary volcanoes poses intermittent hazard. Lahars and pyroclastic flows can devastate local areas, while tephra falls blanket wider regions. Flooding from monsoon rains and volcanic debris dams is recurrent. The population holds no engineered margin against these shocks; survival depends on the capacity to relocate and reoccupy following disruption.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The volcanic soils support productive savanna-woodland with abundant plant foods, tubers, and fruits. The Trinil fauna provides megafaunal protein sources, though access depends on scavenging or opportunistic predation. Water is available in permanent rivers. Stone suitable for flaking is present but scattered; the endowment supports life without encouraging intensive lithic technology. The carrying capacity is moderate to high for a tropical environment.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: At population densities of scattered bands totaling perhaps a few hundred individuals across the region, organic waste and bodily discharge are absorbed without accumulation. Volcanic ash and alluvial sediment continuously bury and reset the surface. No anthropogenic degradation registers at this scale; the sink is effectively unlimited.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Tropical pathogens, intestinal parasites, and vector-borne diseases impose a steady background mortality. Without medicine, infections from wounds, childbirth complications, and epidemic exposures are fatal at rates typical of wild large mammals. Life expectancy at birth is likely below thirty years; few individuals survive past forty.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The Sangiran erectus specimens show robust postcranial build and thick cranial vaults, indicating adequate caloric intake and protein access sufficient for sustained musculoskeletal development. Body mass estimates suggest individuals of 50-60 kg or more. Dental wear patterns indicate coarse, gritty diets incorporating tubers, seeds, and meat. Nutritional stress lines (Harris lines, enamel hypoplasias) appear in some specimens, suggesting episodic shortfall but not chronic famine.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity is limited to the body's own immune response and wound repair, supplemented by whatever wound-tending behaviors can be demonstrated and copied. No pharmacopeia is recorded. Some Sangiran specimens show healed fractures, suggesting survival after injury long enough for bone repair, implying social tolerance of injured individuals during recovery.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Sexual dimorphism in the fossil record suggests polygynous mating systems with larger males competing for access to females. Pair-bonding patterns cannot be reconstructed directly but likely involve prolonged infant dependency given the large brain of erectus relative to body size. Altricial young require extended care, which constrains female foraging mobility.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is low by later standards but represents the densest hominin occupation yet achieved in this region. The Sangiran site complex preserves over one hundred individuals across several hundred thousand years, suggesting continuous occupation by multiple bands totaling perhaps 200-500 individuals in the wider region at any one time. Birth rates must exceed death rates for the population to persist, but growth is slow; the population is at or near local carrying capacity.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: High infant and juvenile mortality means a significant fraction of births do not survive to reproductive age. The elderly dependent load is light, since few reach advanced age. Widows, orphans, and the injured must be absorbed by kin networks or perish; the margin for dependent support is thin.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Foraging provides the subsistence base: gathering plant foods (tubers, fruits, seeds, insects) and procuring animal protein through scavenging and opportunistic hunting. The Trinil fauna includes Stegodon, Axis deer, wild cattle, and large felids; the latter are competitors and predators as much as prey. Household pooling at the band level buffers daily variation. The provisioning floor is above starvation but subject to seasonal and interannual fluctuation.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle is the sole motive power. Fire use is likely present given the global erectus record, providing cooked food, warmth, predator deterrence, and landscape modification. Cooking increases caloric yield from tubers and meat. The energy budget is tight; most captured energy goes to metabolism, with limited surplus for toolmaking or transport.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor organization is informal and kin-based. Sexual division of labor likely exists, with females constrained by infant care and males ranging farther for animal protein. No evidence of coerced labor; cooperation is voluntary and reciprocal within the band.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is for immediate consumption. No durable surplus accumulates beyond a day or two's food. There is no granary, no storage technology, no surplus extraction. The economy is hand-to-mouth at the band scale.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: Body fat is the primary buffer against shortage. No artificial storage containers or food preservation techniques are documented. Risk is pooled through sharing within the band; reciprocity obligations ("share now, owe later") bind individuals to one another.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is limited to intra-band sharing and possibly inter-band gifting during encounters. No markets, no trade routes, no logistics infrastructure. Raw materials are gathered locally; the lithic record shows minimal transport of stone beyond a few kilometers.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of exchange or unit of account. Deferred reciprocity is social, encoded in memory and relationship, not in tokens or records. Obligations are personal and cannot be transferred or accumulated beyond the lifetimes of those who hold them.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: There is no authority capable of extracting surplus. Sharing is by social norm, enforced by reputation and the prospect of future reciprocity. No taxation, tribute, or rent.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Portable wealth is negligible. Status differentials exist based on age, sex, and individual prowess, but material inequality is minimal. Defense of resources is territorial at the band level, maintained by presence and intimidation rather than fortification.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste is scattered at camp sites and reabsorbed by the environment. Bone refuse and flaked stone accumulate in occupation layers but at densities too low to constitute pollution. No waste management problem exists at this scale.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship is the primary organizing principle. Bands likely consist of related individuals centered on a matrilineal or bilateral core, with males dispersing at maturity. Inheritance is biological (genetic) and imitative (behavioral); there is no property to bequeath.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole association. Mutual aid is obligatory within it; sharing food and providing protection are survival necessities, not optional virtues. Inter-band relations are episodic, perhaps hostile, perhaps cooperative depending on kinship ties.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Leisure exists in interstices of the foraging round. Play among juveniles transmits motor skills and social roles. Adults engage in grooming, resting, and social interaction during non-foraging hours. No formal festive spaces or scheduled rituals are documented, but sociability is constant within the band.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status hierarchies are informal, based on age, sex, physical prowess, and perhaps individual reputation as a provider or defender. There are no castes, classes, or hereditary ranks. Group structure is egalitarian in the sense that no formal offices exist, but dominance hierarchies are present as in all social primates.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: There is no administration. Decision-making is by consensus or dominance within the band. No offices, no bureaucracy, no record-keeping. Authority is personal and situational.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Individuals can coerce through physical strength and threat display. The band can collectively exclude or punish defectors. No organized military, no police, no fortifications. Conflict resolution is face-to-face, mediated by kinship and dominance relationships.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is discharged through intra-band conflict (fights, reconciliation), fission of bands when tensions exceed tolerance, and dispersal of individuals. The grievance load is low because material stakes are low. Disorder is self-limiting; a band that cannot maintain cohesion simply splits.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational and personal. An individual who demonstrates skill in a given domain (hunting, defense, foraging knowledge) may lead in that context. No permanent chiefs or formal leaders. Authority derives from demonstrated competence and social relationships.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to kin and band-mates, maintained by ongoing interaction and reciprocity. There is no abstract legitimacy to erode; belonging is immediate and practical.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is limited to tasks the band can accomplish together: group foraging, defense against predators, care of young. The capacity for unified action is high within the band, negligible beyond it. Succession is non-problematic because there are no offices to inherit.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands are probably rare and wary. Posture is defensive; expansion into new territory occurs through fission and dispersal, not conquest. No alliances or coordinated inter-group action is documented.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The emotional baseline is set by daily survival in a predator-rich environment. Vigilance, caution, and social attentiveness are adaptive. Trust within the band is high; trust of outsiders is low or absent. Anxiety about predators, food scarcity, and group membership shapes the emotional landscape.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection leads to departure from the band rather than internal decay. Apathy is not adaptive; individuals who cease contributing are not supported. The affective load is discharged through social interaction and occasional conflict.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is gestural, postural, vocal (non-linguistic), and demonstrative. Imitation is the primary mode of information transfer: skills are shown, not told. The shared code is bodily, not symbolic; it is legible only in person, in real time. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band, where all have grown up watching the same demonstrators. Outsiders would need prolonged exposure to acquire the local behavioral repertoire.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of a walking hominin. There are no signals that outpace the individual. News of distant events arrives only when an individual who witnessed them arrives in person.

Record, Storage & Persistence: There is no external memory. All knowledge is stored in living brains and bodies. When an individual dies, their particular skills and memories die with them. Transmission is lossy; each generation reinvents or loses some fraction of what the previous generation knew.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Without language, there is no discourse to censor. Social norms are enforced through immediate reaction (approval, disapproval, punishment) rather than verbal prohibition. Taboos, if any, are behavioral, not articulated.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by movement, novelty, and social cues. Amplification is personal: a skilled demonstrator can teach many observers, but only those present. There is no broadcast, no virality, no recorded message.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity depends on the fidelity of imitation. Errors introduced by imperfect copying accumulate over generations (the "cultural ratchet" slips backward as well as forward). No verification mechanism exists beyond trial and success.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral intuitions are social-emotional, enforced by feelings of approval and disapproval, fairness and resentment. Reciprocity and kin favoritism are likely foundational. Abstract principles cannot be articulated; right and wrong are felt, not debated.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: There is no law, no code, no written or spoken rule. Behavioral norms are transmitted by example and enforced by social response.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved by dominance, reconciliation, or avoidance. There are no courts, no judges, no formal procedures. Sanction is immediate: exclusion, physical punishment, or withdrawal of cooperation.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: There are no formal rights. Protection is provided by the band to its members as a matter of mutual interest. Compliance is with social expectations, enforced by the continuous presence of others.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: The powerful (physically dominant individuals) can act with relative impunity within the band. Wronged individuals have recourse to alliance-building, retaliation, or departure. There is no accumulating justice deficit because there is no formal justice system to fall short.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no formal inquiry, no theory, no explanatory paradigm. Understanding of the world is practical and implicit: what works is repeated; what fails is abandoned. Cause and effect are grasped at the level of immediate experience, not abstracted into general principles.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical knowledge is embodied in skilled action: how to knap a flake, where to find tubers, how to avoid predators. Method is transmitted by demonstration. The toolkit is simple: minimally worked stone flakes, possibly wooden spears and digging sticks (not preserved), and fire. The famous paucity of lithic artifacts in Java suggests reliance on organic tools (bamboo, wood) that do not survive.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship by observation. Children learn by watching and imitating adults. The knowledge stock is shallow compared to later periods: a finite repertoire of skills, geographically specific, held in living minds. Skill distribution is relatively even; all adults master the basic survival repertoire.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Skills are lost when their practitioners die without demonstrating them to successors. Innovation is rare and often not retained. The cultural ratchet slips; there is no net accumulation of technique across the window, only maintenance of a stable repertoire.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no articulated mythos, no verbal origin story, no historical memory beyond individual lifetimes. Identity is immediate: one belongs to this band, these kin. The "founding" of the group is not conceptualized; the group simply is.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: Without language, there can be no narrative legitimation. The social order is accepted as given, not justified. Authority rests on presence and power, not story.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is sparse: stone flakes, possibly wooden and bamboo tools, fire. No art objects, no ornaments, no pigment use is documented for Javanese erectus. The made-object world is functional, not decorative. Expression, if any, is in gesture, posture, and bodily display.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Without symbolic forms, there is no form exhaustion in the cultural sense. The repertoire of behaviors may become rote, but there is no hollowing of meaning because meaning is not symbolically encoded.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: There is no documented cosmology. Existential outlook, if any, is not articulated. The world is experienced directly, not framed by metaphysical models. Death is observed but not, so far as evidence shows, ritualized.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No evidence of ritual behavior survives. If ritualized actions exist (repeated gestures, coordinated vocalizations), they are not archaeologically visible. The sacred, as a category, may not yet exist.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: There are no religious institutions, no priesthood, no doctrine. Authority in any spiritual domain would be personal and charismatic, not institutionalized.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Without articulated belief systems, there is nothing to diffuse, blend, or displace. The spiritual dimension is, so far as evidence permits, a blank.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: There is no enchantment to lose. The residue of disenchantment does not register because the sacred has not been articulated in a form that can decay.

docs.title: 150,000 BCE – 100,000 BCE — Homo floresiensis Isolation on Flores
docs.text: Summary: Across these fifty millennia the Homo floresiensis population on Flores, separated from the Sunda mainland by deep-water channels that no land bridge ever crosses, completes its evolutionary isolation: body and brain diminish to a third of erectus size while a simple flake technology persists unchanged, a natural experiment in what happens when a hominin lineage is sealed away from gene flow with only imitation to carry its knowledge across generations.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: Flores lies east of the Wallace Line, separated from Sundaland by the Lombok Strait and other deep-water passages that remain submerged even during maximum glacial lowstands. The island is mountainous, volcanically active, and roughly 350 kilometers long. Internal transit is constrained by steep terrain and dense vegetation. The coast offers the only level corridors.

Climate Regime & Volatility: Tropical monsoonal climate prevails, with wet and dry seasons of moderate contrast. Glacial-interglacial cycles affect rainfall intensity but not temperature range; the island remains warm and humid throughout. Forest cover persists with some savanna mosaic in rain-shadow valleys.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: The volcanic chain along Flores poses eruption and lahar risk; ash falls periodically blanket portions of the island. Earthquakes accompany volcanic activity. Flooding occurs in monsoon season. The small population holds no engineered margin against any of these hazards.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The island supports a depauperate fauna: Stegodon florensis insularis (a dwarf elephant), Komodo dragons, giant rats, and various birds. Large predators other than dragons are absent. Plant resources include tropical fruits, tubers, and palms. Freshwater is abundant in streams descending from the volcanic highlands.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: At the population densities involved, anthropogenic waste loads are trivial. Organic refuse decomposes in the tropical climate; bone and stone accumulate in cave deposits without saturating any environmental sink.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Island isolation reduces pathogen diversity relative to the mainland; endemic diseases are present but epidemic sweeps are limited by small population size. Mortality is dominated by trauma, predation, and chronic illness rather than infectious outbreak.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The small body size of Homo floresiensis — approximately one meter tall, 25–30 kilograms — represents an evolved adaptation to island conditions, likely driven by resource limitation. Skeletal remains show robust musculature relative to body size. Dental wear indicates a diet including tough plant foods and meat.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Care is limited to what group members can provide directly. Skeletal evidence suggests individuals survived significant injuries, implying social support through convalescence. No pharmacological knowledge survives except through imitation of observed remedy-seeking behavior.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Small population size constrains mate choice. Inbreeding is likely elevated but not lethal to the population. Pair bonds and extended parental investment persist; juvenile growth is slow relative to body size.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population is very small, perhaps a few hundred individuals across the island. Replacement is slow; the population is stable or slowly declining through the window. Density is low, constrained by island carrying capacity and the absence of mainland gene flow.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Few individuals survive to old age. The dependency load is primarily children; the productive cohort absorbs this load through food sharing. No accumulation of aged dependents occurs.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Foraging provides the provisioning floor. Diet includes dwarf Stegodon (hunted or scavenged), giant rats, birds, and plant foods. There is no cultivation, no storage technology, no surplus beyond immediate consumption. The population lives at or near the margin.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle is the sole power source. Fire use is attested at Liang Bua; hearths indicate cooking and possibly defense against Komodo dragons. No tools amplify energy conversion beyond simple flaked stone and possibly wooden implements.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Division of labor follows age and sex without formal specialization. No coercion exists beyond dominance hierarchies. Labor is mobilized by immediate need and group cohesion.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production equals consumption. Nothing is produced beyond immediate use. The lithic assemblage shows no elaboration across tens of thousands of years, indicating static technical capacity.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: There are no reserves beyond body fat. No caching or storage technology exists. Seasonal or episodic shortage is absorbed through reduced intake and increased mortality.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: No trade exists. Raw materials are locally sourced. The island's isolation precludes exchange with mainland populations.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of value exists. Reciprocity operates through immediate food sharing within the band.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Dominant individuals may claim priority access, but no institutionalized extraction occurs. Redistribution is ad hoc sharing.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: There are no durable assets. Positional advantage is individual and transient.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste decomposes in place. Bone and lithic debris accumulate in caves, forming the archaeological deposits that reveal the population's presence.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship is recognized through maternal bonds and familiarity. No formal rules govern pairing or inheritance. The small population means most individuals are related.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole unit of association. Mutual aid is expressed through food sharing and collective defense. No larger institutions exist.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Play among juveniles transmits skills through imitation. Grooming and proximity maintenance sustain adult bonds. No festive structure is recoverable.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Dominance hierarchies based on physical prowess and age likely exist. Status is individual, not heritable. No castes or permanent factions exist.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists. Decision-making is distributed and immediate.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Coercion is individual and interpersonal. Defense against Komodo dragons may require cooperative action, but no specialized warriors or organized violence is attested.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Conflict resolves through submission, avoidance, or fission. The small population size limits the scope of disorder. Grievance does not accumulate across generations.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal and situational, based on demonstrated competence. No office or title exists.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is to the band, maintained through daily interaction. There is no abstract order requiring legitimation.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is coordinated through imitation and response to dominant individuals. Coordination for hunting or defense occurs without deliberation.

External Relations & Posture: There are no external relations. The population is completely isolated; no other hominin groups exist on Flores during this window.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Affective states are immediate and interpersonal. Trust extends to familiar group members. The small population means all members likely know one another directly.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Individual withdrawal or exhaustion occurs but does not accumulate as a social fact. The band's affective tone resets with personnel change.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is gestural and possibly vocal but not linguistic. Meaning is carried by demonstration. The small population ensures high mutual legibility among all members.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels no faster than an individual can walk. The island's small size means news of a kill or danger can spread within hours to days.

Record, Storage & Persistence: There is no record. Knowledge persists only through overlapping generations of imitation. The unchanging lithic tradition suggests successful intergenerational transmission of at least basic techniques.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: There is no discourse to frame. Communication is situational and immediate.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by social cues and environmental signals. No mechanism for amplification exists.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal fidelity is maintained by continuous demonstration. The stable lithic tradition indicates low noise in technical transmission, though this may reflect simplicity rather than high fidelity.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral intuitions exist but cannot be articulated. Fairness in food sharing and outrage at cheating regulate conduct without codification.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: There is no law or code. Conduct is regulated by immediate social pressure and dominance.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes resolve through force, submission, or avoidance. No third-party adjudication exists.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No rights exist as formal claims. Protection comes from the band's collective interest in each member.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs are addressed or forgotten within the lifespan of the parties. No record maintains accumulated injustice.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no inquiry or theory. Understanding is practical: which foods are safe, where water flows, how to avoid predators.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: A simple Mode 1 flake technology persists unchanged throughout the window. Tools are expedient, made on local volcanic stone, and discarded after use. The technique is adequate for butchery and plant processing but shows no elaboration.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Skills transmit through observation and practice. The knowledge stock is the sum of living practitioners' competencies. The unchanging technology suggests a minimal but stable repertoire.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: The stable lithic tradition indicates techniques are not lost, but there is no innovation to render old methods obsolete. The system is static, neither advancing nor regressing.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no mythos or narrative identity. Identity is immediate: this group, this island, these individuals.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No order requires legitimation. Dominance is self-evident.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: No art survives. Material culture is strictly utilitarian: flaked tools, fire, bone refuse. If symbolic behavior exists, it leaves no trace.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: There are no forms to exhaust. The cultural dimension is minimal.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No cosmology can be attributed. The existential outlook is immediate and practical.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual is attested. Repeated actions may serve social functions but are indistinguishable from practical activity.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: There are no institutions or doctrine.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Complete isolation precludes diffusion or displacement. Whatever beliefs exist are local and invisible to the record.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: The concept does not apply. There is no enchantment to lose, no sacred frame to erode.

docs.title: 120,000 BCE – 70,000 BCE — Late Homo erectus at Ngandong
docs.text: Summary: A terminal Homo erectus population persists along the Solo River terraces of East Java during the late Pleistocene, representing one of the last surviving erectus groups globally; their archaic morphology unchanged across hundreds of millennia, these hominins occupy a narrowing environmental niche as glacial-interglacial oscillations reshape Sundaland's coastlines, their continued existence hinging on the stability of local riverine habitats and the absence of competing hominin lineages.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Ngandong locality occupies alluvial terraces along the Solo River in East Java, a fluvial corridor cutting through the volcanic uplands toward the northern coastal plain; this riverine axis provides reliable water, attracts game to predictable crossings, and offers transport routes through otherwise dense vegetation, reducing spatial friction for groups tethered to the drainage.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The late Pleistocene brings substantial glacial-interglacial swings, with sea levels fluctuating by over 100 meters; during glacial maxima, Java connects via exposed Sundaland to mainland Asia, while interglacial high stands isolate it as an island; tropical temperatures remain warm but monsoonal precipitation patterns shift, affecting forest-savanna mosaics and prey distributions.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: East Java sits within the volcanic arc, exposing inhabitants to ashfall, lahars, and seismic activity; the Toba super-eruption around 74,000 BCE deposits ash across the region, potentially stressing populations through reduced sunlight and vegetation dieback; flooding along the Solo River during heavy monsoons poses additional seasonal hazard.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The Solo River terraces provide access to fresh water year-round, while surrounding mixed woodland and grassland support diverse fauna including Stegodon, bovids, and cervids; volcanic soils are nutrient-rich, sustaining productive vegetation; lithic raw materials remain scarce locally, with most suitable stone occurring in distant volcanic or metamorphic deposits.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: At this population scale and technological level, the environmental sink absorbs all organic waste without detectable stress; bone accumulations at the site represent natural depositional processes rather than pollution; no anthropogenic landscape degradation is evident.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Tropical conditions host endemic parasites and vector-borne diseases, elevating baseline pathogen exposure; without evidence of care facilities or healed trauma consistent with nursing, mortality from infection likely claims individuals before senescence; population turnover remains high.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The robust morphology preserved in Ngandong crania indicates adequate caloric intake to sustain large body mass and thick cranial vaulting; access to riverine protein sources and megafaunal hunting likely provides sufficient nutrition, though seasonal lean periods may impose periodic stress.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity remains limited to innate physiological recovery and whatever rudimentary wound-tending imitation transmits; no evidence of surgical intervention, splinting, or pharmacological treatment exists; survival of serious injury depends on individual constitution and group provisioning during incapacity.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Mating patterns remain unknown but likely involve small-group polygyny consistent with great ape and early hominin comparators; sexual dimorphism in the Ngandong sample suggests male-male competition; reproductive success depends on female foraging returns and male protection and provisioning.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density remains extremely low, perhaps a few hundred individuals across the broader Solo drainage; birth rates sufficient for replacement operate against high infant and juvenile mortality; the population persists but does not expand, suggesting equilibrium at carrying capacity.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Dependent loads include juveniles too young to forage independently and any injured or aged individuals retained in the group; without linguistic instruction, skill transfer requires extended co-residence, prolonging juvenile dependency; mortality likely claims most before extreme old age, limiting elder dependency burden.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Subsistence centers on hunting megafauna and medium-sized mammals at river crossings and along the forest-grassland ecotone, supplemented by gathering plant foods, insects, and freshwater resources; the provisioning floor sits above starvation but offers limited surplus, with seasonal fluctuation in availability.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy capture relies entirely on human muscular effort applied through simple tools; fire use is presumed but not archaeologically demonstrated at Ngandong itself; caloric return rates from hunting large prey provide concentrated energy packets that sustain the robust somatic investment these hominins display.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor organization is informal, embedded in kinship and co-residence; age and sex likely structure task allocation, with males undertaking higher-risk hunting and females focusing on gathering and child transport; coercion operates through social sanction rather than institutionalized hierarchy.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production remains immediate-return foraging with negligible surplus; food cannot be stored effectively in tropical conditions, and no evidence of caching or delayed consumption exists; each day's intake must be secured anew.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: Reserves are held in body fat rather than external storage; the robust erectus physiology may represent a biological buffering strategy against lean seasons; no material storage technology exists.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange, if any, operates within the local band and perhaps between adjacent groups during encounters; no evidence of long-distance raw material transport exists; logistics are limited to daily foraging radius, perhaps 10-20 kilometers.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of exchange or value storage exists; all transactions are immediate or embedded in ongoing social reciprocity; deferred exchange relies on memory of past sharing and expectation of future reciprocation.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Redistribution is informal, occurring through meat-sharing after successful hunts; dominant individuals may claim preferential access, but surplus extraction in any formal sense is absent.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Wealth differentiation is minimal; individuals may possess favored tools or sleeping spots, but accumulation is impossible; defense of territory occurs at the group level against other hominin bands.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Organic waste is left in place and absorbed by scavengers and decomposition; bone accumulations represent natural taphonomic processes; no deliberate waste management exists.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship structures are presumed bilateral and shallow, extending to recognized kin within the co-resident band; inheritance is limited to learned behaviors and any personal tools, transmitted through observation and imitation rather than verbal designation.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band constitutes the primary association, with mutual aid operating through food-sharing, collective vigilance, and cooperative hunting; reciprocity is enforced through co-residence and observation, with defectors losing access to group benefits.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-foraging time is spent in rest, grooming, play, and social interaction; juveniles learn through play-fighting and imitative foraging; sociability maintains group cohesion essential for collective hunting and defense.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status hierarchy exists informally, based on age, physical prowess, and possibly reproductive success; no formalized ranks or hereditary status operate; group structure remains fluid, with fission-fusion dynamics responding to resource availability.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; decision-making is distributed and contextual, emerging from immediate circumstances rather than deliberated governance; leadership is situational and based on demonstrated competence.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Force is wielded individually or collectively through physical strength and simple weapons; no monopoly on violence exists; conflict resolution relies on submission displays, avoidance, or departure rather than adjudication.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through dominance displays, temporary avoidance, or group fission; interpersonal violence likely occurs but leaves no clear skeletal evidence in the Ngandong sample; disorder remains low given small group size and absence of accumulated grievance.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is informal, accruing to individuals who demonstrate hunting success, physical dominance, or social centrality; authority is not heritable and must be continually reaffirmed through performance.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is personal and immediate, based on demonstrated reciprocity and kinship; no abstract authority claims legitimacy; compliance arises from social pressure and mutual benefit rather than ideology.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action emerges in hunting, defense, and group movement; resolve is mobilized through imitation and emotional contagion rather than deliberation; the capacity for sustained coordinated effort is limited by the absence of linguistic planning.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands are likely cautious, ranging from avoidance to occasional interbreeding; hostility toward strangers is probable given competition for territory; no evidence of inter-group alliance or warfare exists.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The emotional baseline is presumed stable, oriented toward survival, social bonding, and reproduction; trust extends within the band to known individuals; stranger anxiety and predator vigilance maintain alertness.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection manifests as departure from the group rather than internal dissent; spent will is not a collective phenomenon at this scale; individual exhaustion or despair would result in abandonment or death.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication relies on gesture, vocalization, facial expression, and postural signaling; no symbolic language exists; mutual intelligibility is high within the band but limited to immediate perceptual contexts; abstract reference and displacement are absent.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of physical co-presence; vocal calls can alert distant band members within auditory range; no transmission occurs beyond direct sensory contact.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external recording medium exists; all information is held in living memory and transmitted through demonstration; knowledge persists only as long as knowledgeable individuals survive and can model behaviors for observers.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Without language, framing and censorship as concepts do not apply; communication is transparent to observers; deception is limited to behavioral concealment rather than verbal misdirection.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by novel stimuli, social signals, and emotionally salient events; amplification occurs through behavioral mimicry and emotional contagion; no mechanisms for deliberate message propagation exist.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is high within close-range interaction; noise enters through ambiguity in gestural communication and observer error in imitative learning; drift accumulates across generations as techniques are imperfectly copied.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Proto-moral intuitions around fairness, reciprocity, and harm are presumed based on primate comparators; these operate through emotional response rather than articulated principle; inequity aversion and punishment of cheaters likely exist in rudimentary form.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No law or codification exists; behavioral norms are transmitted through observation of consequences and social sanction; regulation is continuous with social interaction rather than abstracted from it.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are settled through dominance interaction, submission, or avoidance; liability is not assigned abstractly; sanction consists of aggression, exclusion, or withdrawal of cooperation.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No concept of rights exists; protection derives from group membership and individual capacity; compliance with behavioral norms is enforced through immediate social consequence rather than abstract obligation.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Powerful individuals may act with relative impunity; wrongs are avenged through retaliation or fade with time; no accumulating record of grievance exists beyond individual memory.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry or theory exists; understanding of the world is practical and immediate, oriented toward survival-relevant regularities; causal reasoning is limited to observable sequences without abstraction.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical knowledge centers on tool manufacture (if any lithics are produced), butchery, fire maintenance, and foraging strategies; methods are learned through observation and imitation, with no explicit instruction possible.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education occurs through guided participation and imitative learning; the knowledge stock is limited to what living individuals can demonstrate; skill distribution varies by age and aptitude but is not formally tracked or transmitted.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge is lost when its bearers die without successful transmission; the conservatism of erectus technology over hundreds of millennia suggests minimal innovation and correspondingly minimal obsolescence; techniques are replicated rather than improved.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Without language, narrative identity is absent; memory is episodic and individual; group identity is constituted through co-residence and kinship recognition rather than shared story.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists; the prevailing order is simply the way things are, not justified through story or argument.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture consists of utilitarian objects only; no unambiguous art, ornament, or symbolic marking is associated with Ngandong erectus; aesthetic preference may exist but leaves no archaeological trace.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Without symbolic forms, exhaustion and meaning decay do not apply; material culture remains purely functional and shows no stylistic evolution.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No evidence supports any cosmological framework; existence is presumably experienced without metaphysical reflection; the distinction between sacred and profane is not drawn.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No ritual practice is archaeologically attested; behaviors may carry emotional significance without being ritualized in a recognizably religious sense.
