Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole structure of association. Mutual aid encompasses hunting cooperation, childcare sharing, food distribution, and collective defense. Inter-band contact occurs at seasonal aggregation points, governed by negotiated reciprocity and mating exchange.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Leisure is embedded in daily life: resting around fire, social grooming, play among juveniles, and informal social bonding. No formal leisure category is distinct from work; sociability is continuous.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Stratification is minimal. Status accrues to skilled individuals — successful hunters, knowledgeable elders — but is not heritable or fixed. Material equality prevails; no class or caste division exists. Group structure is egalitarian, constrained by the impossibility of accumulating material advantage.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative capacity exists. Decisions are made collectively through discussion, imitation of leaders, and consensus emergence. No offices, records, or bureaucracy structure authority. Band leadership is situational and impermanent.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: No coercive apparatus exists. All adults are capable of violence; conflict resolution proceeds through social pressure, avoidance, and group fission. Weaponry — stone-tipped spears, thrown projectiles — serves hunting primarily, with interpersonal violence episodic and unorganized.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through band fission and individual departure. Grievance does not accumulate institutionally; it resolves through exit or direct confrontation. No apparatus can decay because none exists. The residue is minimal and cleared by mobility.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is personal and situational: a skilled hunter leads during the hunt, a knowledgeable elder guides migration. Authority derives from demonstrated competence and cannot be institutionalized or inherited. Influence is exercised through example rather than command.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is direct and personal — loyalty to band-mates and kin. No abstract legitimacy exists; belonging is enacted through presence, sharing, and mutual support. Defection or failure to reciprocate dissolves allegiance immediately.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective will coalesces around immediate tasks: the hunt, camp relocation, defense. Mobilization is achieved through imitation and emotional contagion. No succession contest exists because no permanent office is contested. Will forms situationally and dissolves after action.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands range from avoidance to cautious exchange to episodic conflict. Territorial boundaries are flexible; intrusion triggers confrontation if detected, but exclusive defense is impractical for mobile groups. No alliance structures persist beyond temporary cooperation.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Sentiment fluctuates with subsistence success, interpersonal relations, and external threat. Trust is high within kin groups, attenuating toward strangers. Behavioral temper is alert and pragmatic; vigilance is continuous. The emotional baseline is cautious cooperation within familiar groups.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Spent will manifests as withdrawal, reduced participation, or departure. Disaffection feeds group fission rather than internal decay. The residue clears through mobility; nothing accumulates institutionally.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is pre-linguistic or proto-linguistic: gesture, vocalization, facial expression, and bodily demonstration carry meaning. Large brain size may support more complex signaling than earlier populations, but no evidence distinguishes the Xujiayao communication system from imitative predecessors. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band, low with outsiders.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Transmission is face-to-face, limited to shouting distance and walking speed. Nothing travels faster than a messenger can walk; spatial reach of information is bounded by the group's movement range. No amplification technology exists.

Record, Storage & Persistence: All information is stored in living memory. No external record exists; knowledge is lost with its carrier unless transmitted beforehand. The group's entire cognitive inheritance depends on successful imitation before death removes the source.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: No institutional framing or censorship exists. Discourse norms are social: topics and behaviors approved or disapproved by group reaction. The communicable domain is limited by the imitative code rather than prohibition.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Reception is direct; attention tracks immediate relevance — threats, opportunities, social interactions. Amplification is limited to imitation: a useful behavior spreads only as fast as individuals observe and copy it.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is high within the small group; direct observation minimizes distortion. Drift accumulates across generations as imitation introduces small errors. No verification or correction mechanism exists; fidelity depends on redundant demonstration and practice.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Justice is felt intuitively and reciprocally: fairness is enacted through sharing, cheating punished by exclusion or retaliation. No explicit moral code is articulated; right and wrong are experienced directly in emotional response to behavior.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No law exists. Conduct is governed by custom transmitted through imitation — the way things are done, replicated generation to generation with slow drift. Reform is unintentional; change accumulates through copying error and environmental pressure.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved through direct confrontation, elder intervention, or group pressure. Sanction ranges from shaming through exclusion to physical violence. No procedure formalizes adjudication; outcomes depend on power, alliances, and social capital.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Rights are not articulated but enacted: members expect reciprocal treatment and punish deviation. Compliance burden is minimal — conformity to sharing norms and participation in collective activity. Individual autonomy within these bounds is high.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Impunity exists for the strong or when violations go unwitnessed. Wrong may remain unredressed when victims lack allies. The gap is managed through exit and avoidance rather than accumulated grievance.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry exists. Understanding is practical and procedural: knowing how to make tools, track animals, navigate terrain. No explanatory paradigm is articulated; causal reasoning is intuitive and embedded in technique.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: The Xujiayao lithic industry shows sophisticated prepared-core techniques and systematic blank production. Tool standardization indicates shared mental templates transmitted through observation and practice. Technical method is advanced relative to earlier periods, though the transmission mode remains imitative.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship through observation; juveniles watch and imitate adults, corrected by guidance. The knowledge stock is distributed across the adult population; specialists emerge by aptitude rather than formal role. Stock attrition through death of carriers is continuous.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Obsolete techniques are shed as their practitioners die without transmitting them. Knowledge decay is constant; each generation inherits a filtered subset of the previous. Error accumulates uncorrected; innovation is slow and accidental.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Identity is band-based and immediate — we are those who share this fire, eat together, know each other. Memory extends only as far as living recall; no foundational narrative is articulated because articulation requires language. Origin is presence rather than story.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No explicit ideology exists. The order is self-legitimating through repetition: this is how things are done because they have always been done this way. Legitimacy is habit enacted rather than argument delivered.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is utilitarian: stone tools, bone implements, fire features. No clearly symbolic artifacts are recovered from Xujiayao; if expressive objects exist, they are perishable or unrecognizable. The made-object world is functional and sparse.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Form exhaustion does not apply where elaborated symbolic forms have not developed. Meaning is situational and immediate; no symbolic repertoire exists to hollow out. The baseline is static rather than depleted.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: Cosmology is implicit and unarticulated. The world contains animals, plants, weather, and other humans, encountered directly. No metaphysical framework distinguishes natural from supernatural; existential orientation is practical and immediate.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No unambiguous ritual is evidenced materially. If proto-ritual exists, it is indistinguishable from routine social behavior. Devotion, if felt, leaves no recoverable trace in the archaeological record.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists. No doctrine is transmitted. If spiritual authority exists, it is personal and indistinguishable from prestige in other domains.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Spiritual belief, to the extent it exists, is local and stable. No mechanism for diffusion or displacement operates beyond the slow drift of imitation. Nothing is recorded; transmission depends entirely on co-presence.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment cannot occur where the sacred has not been distinguished and articulated. If sacred experience exists, it is immanent in ordinary life rather than a separate domain that could erode. No residue of lost transcendence accumulates.

docs.title: 400,000 BCE – 250,000 BCE — Middle Pleistocene Regional Diversity
docs.text: Summary: Multiple hominin populations occupy distinct ecological niches across the Yellow and Yangtze basins during the Middle Pleistocene, from the Hexian cave system in the south to the Nanjing area and continuing occupation at Zhoukoudian in the north; the defining condition is geographic fragmentation imposed by the Qinling Mountains and varied terrain that channels populations into semi-isolated regional clusters, each developing localized technological and behavioral repertoires transmitted through imitation within groups but drifting apart between them.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Yellow and Yangtze basins present a mosaic of distinct landscape units — the Loess Plateau in the northwest, the North China Plain in the center, the mountainous interior, and the lower Yangtze valley in the southeast — each imposing different constraints on movement and settlement; the Qinling Mountains bisect the region along an east-west axis, creating a major barrier between northern and southern populations; river valleys and intermontane basins provide corridors within regions while mountain ranges channel and impede long-distance movement between them.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The window spans multiple glacial-interglacial oscillations within Marine Isotope Stages 11 through 8, with interglacials bringing warm temperate conditions and expanded forest cover while glacials push steppe grasslands southward and reduce annual precipitation; the monsoon system's strength fluctuates, with interglacial strengthening bringing reliable summer rains to the southeast and glacial weakening shifting the effective moisture boundary southward; seasonal temperature ranges remain continental, with cold dry winters and warm humid summers across most of the region.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Flooding along major river courses poses recurrent hazards during monsoon peaks; the Loess Plateau experiences ongoing erosion and occasional catastrophic slumping; seismic activity along fault systems in the western highlands creates periodic earthquake risk; the hazard regime favors occupation of elevated terraces and cave sites that provide shelter from both flooding and seismic collapse.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Lithic raw materials vary by region — quartzite and flint in the Nihewan area, limestone and quartz in karst regions, volcanic rocks near ancient eruption sites — with local availability shaping technological practice more than shared tradition; energy derives entirely from direct solar capture through the food web, with no evidence of systematic fire management beyond the practices established at Zhoukoudian; game abundance and plant productivity fluctuate with glacial-interglacial cycles.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: At population densities measured in tens of individuals per occupied territory, waste and refuse accumulate only at concentrated occupation sites; cave deposits at Hexian and continuing Zhoukoudian occupation show thick stratigraphic accumulation of bone refuse and lithic debitage indicating repeated use over millennia; open-air camps leave ephemeral traces quickly dispersed by natural processes; the landscape absorbs all human discharge without measurable saturation.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic disease exposure remains tied to local conditions — parasitic loads from game consumption, water-borne pathogens from contaminated sources, zoonotic transmission from prey species; the geographic fragmentation limits epidemic spread between regions; baseline mortality remains high, with few individuals surviving past the fourth decade; skeletal evidence from the period shows trauma, arthritis, and dental disease as common conditions.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Dietary breadth varies by region, with northern populations relying heavily on large herbivores (horse, deer, rhinoceros) while southern populations exploit more diverse resources including smaller game and possibly freshwater species; seasonal nutritional stress leaves no direct skeletal evidence from this window but is assumed from environmental conditions; brain size and body robustness indicate adequate protein and caloric intake for normal hominin development during non-stress periods.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity rests entirely on individual physiology and group tolerance of injured members; some skeletal evidence from other Middle Pleistocene sites shows healed fractures indicating survival through recovery periods requiring group support; wound care and treatment of illness proceed by showing and copying within groups, with no capacity to transmit healing knowledge beyond face-to-face demonstration.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Reproductive patterns remain invisible in the record; population replacement must match mortality for regional populations to persist across the 150,000-year window; the semi-isolation of regional populations may concentrate breeding within limited gene pools while occasional contact between neighboring groups introduces genetic variation; pairing dynamics are entirely speculative for this period.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population densities remain extremely low — perhaps a few hundred individuals total across the entire region at any given time — with each regional cluster comprising only a handful of breeding adults and their offspring; the multiple occupied sites (Hexian, Nanjing, Zhoukoudian, others) indicate successful regional persistence rather than high density; demographic renewal proceeds at replacement rates sufficient to maintain but not expand populations.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: The dependency load remains minimal given short lifespans and low population density; injured or aged individuals either recover and contribute or die relatively quickly; the absence of specialized care infrastructure means dependency cannot accumulate beyond what mobile groups can physically carry or tolerate; orphaned young must be absorbed by remaining group members or perish.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Provisioning depends on hunting medium to large game supplemented by plant gathering; the evidence from Hexian and contemporaneous sites shows exploitation of elephant, rhinoceros, deer, and smaller mammals; provisioning remains local, with each group dependent on resources within a few days' travel of occupied sites; the floor sits close to the edge during glacial phases when game concentrates but plant resources diminish.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy capture proceeds through human metabolism alone — the chase, the butchery, the transport of meat to processing locations; fire use for cooking and warmth continues from the Zhoukoudian tradition where groups maintain that knowledge, but the extent of fire use across all regional populations remains uncertain from the archaeological record; no animal labor or mechanical advantage beyond simple tools.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor organization follows the natural division of a small foraging band — those capable of hunting hunt, those capable of gathering gather, those too young or old contribute what they can; coercion operates through the immediate social pressure of a face-to-face group rather than any formal structure; task allocation proceeds by demonstration and imitation rather than verbal instruction or command.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Stone tool production continues at each site using locally available materials; the Hexian assemblage shows continued use of core-and-flake technology with some regional variation from northern industries; no surplus production is possible beyond the immediate needs of the group; each successful hunt produces a temporary surplus of meat that must be consumed before spoilage or shared to build reciprocal obligations.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No durable storage exists; meat must be consumed within days unless dried or frozen by natural conditions; the only buffer against scarcity is body fat accumulated during abundant periods and the social obligation of reciprocity within the group; groups facing local resource failure must move or perish.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange operates only within face-to-face groups; evidence of exotic raw materials is minimal, suggesting lithic procurement remains local; the geographic fragmentation of regional populations limits inter-group exchange, though occasional contact must occur for populations to avoid genetic isolation; logistics extend only as far as a group can walk carrying its possessions and dependents.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: Deferred exchange operates through embodied memory of reciprocal obligations — who shared with whom, who owes whom — with no external tokens or records; this social memory constitutes the only form of value storage, erased when the holders die; the temporal horizon of obligation extends no further than the lifespan of the parties involved.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Within-group sharing distributes meat and other resources according to social relationships and immediate need; dominant individuals may claim priority access but extraction operates through personal relationships rather than institutional forms; no extraction apparatus exists beyond the band itself.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Material wealth consists entirely of carried tools and immediate access to group resources; individuals possess nothing that requires defense beyond the daily radius of group protection; there is no concentration of wealth because there is nothing durable to concentrate.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Lithic debitage accumulates at knapping sites; bone refuse piles at butchering and consumption locations; fire hearths leave ash deposits where fire is used; all waste remains where produced or is naturally dispersed; no routing decisions are required at these population densities.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship structures remain invisible but must exist in some form to organize mating, childcare, and resource sharing; inheritance consists only of learned behavior transmitted through imitation from elder to younger within the group; biological kinship presumably structures who tolerates whom and who helps whom within the small band.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band itself constitutes the entire associational structure — all mutual aid occurs within this face-to-face group; inter-group cooperation beyond the band remains rare and circumstantial; the geographic separation of regional populations limits association to local contexts.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-subsistence time allows for social grooming, play among young, and repetitive practice of technical skills; fire circles where maintained may concentrate evening sociability; the absence of language limits sociability to physical presence and shared activity rather than narrative or abstract communication.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status hierarchies exist within bands based on age, skill, and physical capability; the most skilled knappers and successful hunters command respect and imitation; no formal stratification exists because groups lack the scale and permanence to support it; the regional populations represent parallel groups rather than hierarchical organization.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; the band organizes itself through face-to-face interaction and immediate demonstration; decisions emerge from individual actions that others follow or ignore; leadership operates through demonstrated competence that attracts imitation rather than formal authority.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Force operates through personal confrontation within the band; an adult hominin armed with stone tools can threaten or harm others but no organized coercive apparatus exists; inter-group violence likely occurs at territorial boundaries but leaves no clear archaeological signature in this window.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through physical confrontation, departure from the group, or death; with no permanent institutions, there is no institutional decay; the geographic fragmentation of regional populations may reflect accumulated fission events as groups split rather than managing internal conflict.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leaders emerge through demonstrated competence — successful hunting, effective toolmaking, knowledge of the landscape — and attract followers through imitation rather than command; personal authority extends only as far as others choose to follow; there is no mechanism to institutionalize leadership beyond individual reputation.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Legitimacy operates through the immediate bonds of kinship and familiarity; individuals remain with their groups because that is where they know people and are known; the concept of rule or formal authority has no application at this scale and stage.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action emerges from individual decisions that align — to move camp, to pursue game, to avoid danger — without formal coordination mechanisms; the will of the group is simply the aggregated choices of individuals who can observe each other's actions; there is no mechanism to mobilize group action beyond the example of leading individuals.

External Relations & Posture: Relations between regional populations remain rare and wary; occasional contact for mating or resource sharing must occur but likely involves caution, display, and potential violence; there is no diplomacy, only the immediate assessment of threat or opportunity when strangers meet.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The affective life of these populations remains entirely speculative; solidarity within small groups must be sufficient to maintain cooperation despite the costs of sharing; fear and wariness toward unfamiliar individuals or groups likely shapes inter-population contact; the baseline emotional register probably includes the full range of hominin affects — attachment, jealousy, grief, anger — expressed through body language and vocalization rather than language.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: In such small groups, disaffection expresses itself through departure or death rather than accumulating as a social condition; the emotional residue of failed cooperation or internal conflict disperses with group fission; there is no mechanism for disaffection to persist as a structural feature.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication proceeds through gesture, demonstration, vocalization, and physical guidance — hand guiding hand as the defining mode; the shared code operates within groups that learn together but diverges between groups that develop in isolation; regional populations may accumulate communicative differences that impede mutual understanding.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of human movement — a few kilometers per day — and reaches only those present to witness it; there are no channels beyond direct observation; knowledge of distant events or conditions arrives only when individuals who witnessed them travel to share their presence.

Record, Storage & Persistence: All information storage occurs in living memory; when knowledgeable individuals die, their knowledge dies with them unless they have successfully transmitted it through demonstration to others; there is no external record; accumulated group knowledge persists only through continuous chains of showing and copying, degrading with each transmission.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Without language, framing and censorship operate only through physical control of access to observation — preventing someone from watching a demonstration — or social exclusion from group activities; discourse norms in any linguistic sense do not exist.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention concentrates on the demonstrator during skill transmission; amplification occurs when multiple observers witness the same demonstration and then imitate; there is no mechanism for a message to spread beyond those physically present at its original expression.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Each transmission through imitation introduces variation — the drift that accumulates across generations; there is no mechanism to verify fidelity or correct errors except through the consequences of failed technique; knowledge degrades continuously unless refreshed by successful practice.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The moral sense operates through immediate emotional response — anger at cheating, satisfaction at fair sharing, disgust at violations of group norms — without abstract articulation; what feels wrong is wrong, enforced through social reaction rather than codified rule.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No codification exists or is possible without language; behavioral norms exist as patterns that individuals learn through imitation and social feedback; the closest analog to law is the consistency of group response to certain behaviors, learned through observation rather than instruction.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes resolve through immediate confrontation, submission, or departure; there is no third-party adjudication beyond the reactions of other group members present; sanction operates through ostracism, physical retaliation, or exclusion from sharing — all immediate and personal.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: There are no formal rights; protection comes from kinship bonds and group membership; the compliance burden consists of maintaining the behaviors that keep one in good standing with the group — participating in sharing, avoiding behaviors that provoke retaliation.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: The strong may act with impunity against the weak within groups; wrongs may go unredressed if the wronged party lacks allies or physical capability for retaliation; there is no mechanism for justice beyond immediate social response; grievances not discharged through confrontation simply persist until parties separate or die.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no formal inquiry or theory; understanding of the world develops through individual experience and observation, shared through demonstration where relevant to practical activity; causal understanding extends only to immediately observable relationships — striking flint produces sharp edges, fire produces heat, certain plants cause sickness.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical knowledge resides in practiced motor skills transmitted through imitation; the regional variation in lithic industries reflects accumulated drift in technique as populations develop in isolation; each regional cluster maintains its own technical repertoire, neither more nor less sophisticated than others but locally adapted to available materials and accumulated practice.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education proceeds through observation and imitation with occasional physical guidance; the knowledge stock of each group represents the accumulated practical wisdom of its living members; skill distribution follows individual aptitude and opportunity for practice; some individuals achieve greater proficiency through practice and natural ability, becoming centers of imitation.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays continuously through transmission error and the death of skilled practitioners; techniques that fail produce obvious consequences and may be abandoned; techniques that succeed persist through continued practice; there is no mechanism to recover lost knowledge except through independent rediscovery.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Without language, there is no narrative mythos; identity consists of being a member of this particular group in this particular place; collective memory extends no further than the oldest living member's personal experience; there is no story of origins, only the lived reality of present association.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists in any articulable form; the order legitimates itself through simply being the way things are done — the inertia of learned behavior rather than justified belief.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture consists of functional tools with regional stylistic variation that reflects accumulated drift in learned techniques rather than conscious expression; there is no clear evidence of symbolic or decorative elaboration in this window; the material signature of each regional population serves unintentionally as its cultural marker.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Without symbolic meaning, there is no meaning to decay; the functional adequacy of techniques determines their persistence; forms exhaust themselves only when they cease to work, not when they cease to mean.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: Without language, there is no articulable cosmology; whatever sense of the world's nature exists remains locked in individual minds and shared only through the parallel experience of living together; existential questions in any philosophical sense cannot be formulated or transmitted.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: There is no evidence of ritual practice or sacred behavior in this window; whether repetitive behaviors that might constitute proto-ritual exist remains invisible to archaeology; the sacred as a marked-off domain of experience leaves no trace.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institutions exist; there is no doctrine because there is no language to formulate doctrine; spiritual authority in any formal sense has no application.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Without articulable belief systems, there is nothing to diffuse, blend, or displace; whatever inchoate spiritual sensibilities individuals may hold remain private and perish with them.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: There is no enchantment in any recoverable sense, therefore no disenchantment; the spiritual residue of this period is absence — not the loss of meaning but its never-yet-existence in transmissible form.

docs.title: 1,400,000 BCE – 1,000,000 BCE — Oldowan-like Industry Spread across the Loess Plateau
docs.text: Summary: A four-hundred-thousand-year expansion of simple core-and-flake technology from the Nihewan Basin southwestward across the accumulating loess deposits of northern China, as hominin populations colonize new drainage systems and adapt knapping routines to locally available stone. The binding constraint is imitative transmission without language: each technique persists only so long as a living practitioner demonstrates it and a watching novice copies the gesture; knowledge cannot be articulated, debated, or stored outside the bodies that carry it. The trend documents the capacity of imitation to conserve and spread a rudimentary technology across vast distances and millennia, while revealing its limits — the toolkit remains essentially unchanged because no mechanism exists to propose or evaluate alternatives. The emerging Lantian area in the Wei River drainage marks the southwestern frontier of this expansion.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Loess Plateau extends from the Nihewan Basin in the northeast across Shaanxi and Gansu, a corrugated terrain of wind-deposited silt cut by steep ravines draining toward the Yellow River. The plateau surface rises from 1,000 to over 2,000 meters, creating elevation gradients that channel movement along river valleys. The Wei River corridor, draining eastward through the Qinling-Huaihe line, provides the primary transit route into central China; northward, the Fen and Sang-Gan rivers link the plateau interior to the Nihewan lowlands. Loess accumulation is continuous, burying and preserving occupation surfaces in stratified sequences.

Climate Regime & Volatility: Early Pleistocene climate oscillates between cooler-drier and warmer-wetter phases on 41-kyr orbital cycles, but the amplitude is moderate compared to later periods. The Loess Plateau lies at the northern limit of the East Asian monsoon, making it sensitive to shifts in monsoon penetration. During wetter phases, gallery forests extend along drainage corridors; during drier phases, steppe-grassland dominates interfluves. Interannual variability is high, with monsoon failure producing multi-year droughts that stress both vegetation and dependent fauna.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Loess is prone to catastrophic erosion during intense rainfall, producing debris flows and gully collapse that bury or destroy occupation sites. Seismic activity along the Ordos block margins poses additional hazard. Volcanic activity is minimal in this region, though distant eruptions occasionally deposit tephra markers useful for correlation.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Raw material for knapping derives primarily from river gravels — quartzite, vein quartz, and occasional chert cobbles transported by Pleistocene rivers from upland sources. Quality varies: Nihewan assemblages exploit fine-grained basalt and quartzite; further southwest, coarser materials predominate. Raw material availability constrains the complexity of reduction sequences and the standardization of end products.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Continuous loess deposition buries anthropogenic debris rapidly, preventing accumulation and preserving sites in stratified context. Population densities are far too low to approach any threshold of landscape modification; the physical residue is negligible.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Hominin mortality is shaped by trauma, predation, and endemic parasites rather than epidemic disease. The continental climate reduces vector-borne disease pressure compared to tropical settings, but cold-season stress adds its own mortality burden. Life expectancy is short, with few individuals surviving past the fourth decade.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Early Pleistocene hominins in this region are robust, with body plans adapted to high activity levels and variable food supply. Dietary evidence from associated fauna and site distributions suggests a mixed strategy: plant foods where available, supplemented by scavenging and opportunistic hunting of medium-sized mammals. Nutritional stress during lean seasons is reflected in the intensive processing of carcasses for marrow.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity is limited to the body's regenerative processes and whatever incidental care group proximity affords. No material evidence of deliberate medical treatment survives; survival of injured individuals depends on band tolerance and continued mobility.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Reproductive biology follows early Homo patterns: extended juvenile dependency, prolonged interbirth intervals, and probable multi-male investment in offspring provisioning. Pair-bonding, if present, is loosely structured.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is extremely low, with bands of perhaps fifteen to thirty individuals occupying home ranges of hundreds of square kilometers. Replacement is slow; local extirpation during adverse climatic phases is common, with recolonization from refugia when conditions improve. The trend reflects net population expansion as new territories are colonized, but the process is punctuated by repeated contractions.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: High infant and juvenile mortality absorbs most reproductive output. Adult lifespans are short, and few aged dependents accumulate; the productive cohort bears a modest dependency load that rises sharply during resource shortfalls.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Provisioning rests on daily foraging for plant foods — roots, tubers, fruits, seeds — supplemented by scavenging carcasses and opportunistic capture of small game. Stone tools extend access to marrow and adhering tissue, slightly widening the caloric floor. The subsistence margin is narrow; multi-day shortfalls are common during drought or winter.

Energy Capture & Conversion: All energy derives from human muscle and, possibly, controlled fire, though direct evidence of fire use in this window is ambiguous. The charred materials at some Nihewan sites may reflect natural or anthropogenic burning; no structured hearths are documented. Per-capita energy throughput remains at the hominoid baseline.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Division of labor is minimal, likely structured by age and sex differences in foraging focus. No coercion beyond immediate dominance interactions exists; cooperation is kin-based and reciprocal.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is confined to stone tools and perishable items that leave no trace. The Oldowan-like industry comprises simple cores, unretouched flakes, and occasional choppers — expedient tools made as needed and discarded after use. Surplus accumulation is negligible.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No food storage technology exists. Body fat reserves and cached carcass parts are the only buffers, and neither survives beyond days. The absence of storage exposes bands to every shortfall.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange, if present, is limited to immediate sharing within the band. Raw material transport extends a few kilometers at most; there is no evidence of inter-band trade or logistics networks.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: Deferred reciprocity within kin networks is the only form of value storage. No symbolic tokens or standardized medium exist; obligations are personal and immediate.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Redistribution operates through face-to-face sharing at the moment of acquisition. No formalized extraction exists.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Material inequality is absent; personal possessions are limited to tools in hand. Asset defense is nonexistent because there are no accumulated assets.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Knapping debris, broken tools, and food refuse are abandoned in place, buried by loess accumulation. No waste routing or management exists; the residue is absorbed by natural sedimentation.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: The band is structured by kinship, likely matrilineal with male dispersal at maturity. Inheritance is social rather than material: children inherit access to kin networks and proximity to skill-holders, not property.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole associational unit. Mutual aid obligations bind members through reciprocal sharing and coalitional support; no institutions beyond the band exist.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Rest periods afford grooming and juvenile play, which serve socialization and motor-skill development. No material correlates of leisure activities survive.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status hierarchy is informal, based on age, sex, and individual dominance. No institutionalized stratification exists; influence is personal and situational.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: Formal administration is absent. Coordination arises from immediate signals, leadership by example, and habitual movement patterns learned through co-residence.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Coercion is limited to individual aggression using body and opportunistic objects. No organized weaponry or collective violence apparatus exists.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through dominance displays, submission, grooming reconciliation, and emigration. The band is too small and short-lived to accumulate institutional decay; the residue clears with each generation.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational and informal, arising from demonstrated competence in a given context rather than from fixed office.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is personal and immediate, tied to kinship and familiarity. No abstract authority exists to command or lose legitimacy.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is limited to coordinated foraging, predator response, and group movement. Large-scale mobilization is beyond the band's capacity.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands range from avoidance to wary encounter to aggression. No stable alliances or permanent hostilities exist; posture is determined by immediate circumstance.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Behavioral temper is cautious and risk-averse, shaped by predation pressure and resource uncertainty. Trust extends only to close kin and familiar band members.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection manifests as emigration or marginalization. Spent will clears through fission and dispersal rather than accumulating as collective resentment; the residue is transient.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is pre-linguistic, relying on gesture, vocalization, facial expression, and postural cues. The shared code allows coordination and imitative learning but excludes symbolic content or displaced reference. Mutual intelligibility is high within bands, attenuated across distant groups.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at walking speed through face-to-face encounter. Knowledge of distant resources or hazards depends on mobile individuals who have witnessed them; transmission cannot outrun movement.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists. All knowledge resides in living memory; the Oldowan-like template persists only because each generation copies what the previous generation demonstrates. Loss of skilled practitioners is permanent knowledge loss.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Framing is limited to attentional cues — gaze direction, pointing, alarm calls. No capacity for propositional discourse, censorship, or explicit prohibition exists.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Reception depends on proximity and attention during demonstration. There is no mechanism for amplification beyond the range of direct perception.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is maintained by functional feedback — tools that fail to work are abandoned, techniques that produce working tools are copied. Drift accumulates slowly because imitative fidelity is high, but the system cannot self-correct against accumulated error; the residue is gradual divergence across isolated populations.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Proto-moral intuitions — aversion to cheating, expectation of reciprocity, distress at unfair distribution — are present but not codified. Enforcement is immediate and personal.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No law or codified rule exists. Behavioral norms are transmitted implicitly through observation and corrective response.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved through dominance, submission, or avoidance. There is no third-party adjudication; liability is personal.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is constrained by group context rather than by formal rights. Compliance burden is negligible.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs that exceed the victim's capacity for retaliation go unaddressed. Impunity accretes where dominance shields transgression, but the accumulation clears with mortality.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no inquiry in the propositional sense. Understanding is procedural, embedded in motor routines, and incapable of abstraction or generalization.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: The Oldowan-like industry — simple core reduction, hard-hammer percussion, expedient flake production — represents the technological baseline. Knappers strike cobbles to produce sharp-edged flakes useful for cutting; cores are discarded when exhausted. The method is effective but unstandardized, with high variability in end products depending on raw material quality and individual skill. No prepared-core techniques exist; each reduction is ad hoc.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Skill transmission is purely imitative, requiring close observation and repeated practice in the presence of a skilled practitioner. Knowledge cannot be stored, sent ahead, or retrieved; distribution is limited to those who witness the act. The expansion of industry across the Loess Plateau reflects the spread of practitioners, not the spread of instructions.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge loss is catastrophic and irreversible. If a band loses its skilled knappers without transmission, the technique vanishes locally. The residue is discontinuity — gaps in the archaeological record where populations failed and recolonizers brought new (or recovered) knowledge.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no mythos in the narrative sense. Group identity is experiential and immediate, tied to familiar faces, places, and routines. Memory spans living generations only.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists. The social order is self-evident and unquestioned because there is no capacity to question it through articulated alternatives.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is limited to expedient stone tools and perishable objects. There is no evidence of decorative modification; artifact form is dictated by raw material constraints and functional requirements.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Without symbolic content, there is no meaning to exhaust. Forms persist unchanged until environmental or demographic disruption breaks the transmission chain; the residue is stasis, not decay.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No cosmology exists in the propositional sense. The world is encountered directly, without explanatory framework or metaphysical overlay.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: There is no evidence of ritual or sacred practice. Behavior is instrumental and immediate; no distinction between practical and sacred activity can be recovered.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: Religious institutions are absent by definition. No doctrine, hierarchy, or sacred office exists.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Without spiritual content, there is nothing to diffuse, blend, or displace.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: There is no enchantment to lose. The imitative substrate cannot generate or transmit cosmological propositions; the spiritual residue is blank.

docs.title: 100,000 BCE – 50,000 BCE — Terminal Archaic Populations and Modern Human Arrival
docs.text: Summary: A fifty-thousand-year trend of population turnover across the Yellow and Yangtze basins, as resident late archaic Homo populations — large-brained descendants of the Xujiayao lineage — encounter expanding Homo sapiens groups entering from the south and west; the single most causal factor is the demographic and behavioral edge carried by incoming modern humans, whose imitative repertoires and social cohesion gradually displace or absorb the archaic substrate without catastrophic rupture.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The basin system remains bisected by the Qinling-Huaihe climatic divide; the Loess Plateau in the northwest grades into the alluvial plains of the middle Yellow River, while the Yangtze corridor provides a southern transit axis linking western highlands to the coastal lowlands; river valleys and intermontane basins continue to channel movement, funneling both archaic and incoming modern populations into shared resource zones where encounter is most likely.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The window spans Marine Isotope Stages 5 to early Stage 3, oscillating between warm interglacial phases and cooler stadials; monsoon intensity fluctuates, periodically expanding or contracting the forest-grassland boundary across the Loess Plateau; during cooler phases the northern steppe expands southward, compressing habitable woodland corridors and intensifying competition for refugia.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: Seismic activity along the Qinling fault system and periodic Loess Plateau dust storms remain background hazards; flooding along the middle Yangtze and Yellow rivers punctuates habitation, forcing episodic relocations; no single catastrophic event dominates the record, but cumulative environmental volatility selects for mobile, flexible subsistence.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Abundant quartzite, quartz, and chert sources remain accessible across both basins; faunal communities shift with climate, with large herbivores — horse, deer, bovids — tracking vegetation zones; raw material availability imposes no hard ceiling, though quality varies regionally, favoring certain workshop locales over others.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Human population densities remain low; no evidence of anthropogenic landscape degradation; the physical sink absorbs all discard without saturation; residue is effectively nil.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic parasites and zoonotic exposure persist; mortality from injury, infection, and childbirth remains high; no evidence of epidemic-scale disease, though interbreeding between archaic and modern populations may introduce novel pathogen exposures in contact zones.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Both archaic and modern populations exploit mixed diets of hunted game and gathered plants; skeletal evidence from archaic sites shows robust build and heavy musculature; incoming Homo sapiens display lighter gracile frames but comparable stature; nutritional stress markers are present but not dominant in either group.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Care remains embedded in kinship bands; healed fractures in archaic remains indicate deliberate tending of injured individuals; knowledge of wound treatment and plant remedies persists through imitative transmission, vulnerable to loss with each death of an experienced caretaker.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Both populations are fully capable of interbreeding; genetic evidence from later periods indicates limited but real gene flow between archaic Denisovan-related populations and incoming Homo sapiens; pairing likely follows small-band patterns with exogamous exchange between neighboring groups.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Modern humans gradually increase in density across the window, while archaic populations thin; replacement is slow — measured in millennia rather than generations; no single collapse event, but cumulative demographic attrition favors the expanding sapiens population.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Small band sizes mean dependent individuals — elderly, injured, orphaned — must be absorbed by productive members or perish; neither population escapes this constraint; residue is biologically cleared through mortality rather than social accumulation.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Both archaic and modern populations operate as mobile foragers; hunting provides the bulk of calories in northern zones, with gathering more significant along the Yangtze corridor; provisioning remains precarious, tied to seasonal game movements and plant availability; no evidence of storage beyond immediate consumption.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle remains the sole motive force; fire use continues from Middle Pleistocene traditions, employed for warmth, cooking, and possibly landscape management; per-capita energy throughput is low but sufficient for mobile foraging subsistence.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor is organized within kin bands without coercion beyond kinship obligation; task division by age and sex follows imitative learning; no evidence of surplus extraction or hierarchical command; cooperation is maintained through reciprocity and shared imitative repertoires.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is limited to immediate consumption and tool manufacture; no durable surplus accumulates; the economy operates at the edge of subsistence with minimal buffer against seasonal shortfalls.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: Reserves are embodied in body fat and cached meat; no granaries, no formal storage structures; buffering capacity is thin, absorbed through mobility and band fusion during scarcity.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is limited to adjacent bands; raw materials occasionally move tens of kilometers, indicating some inter-band transfer; no long-distance trade networks; logistics are constrained by human portage and the absence of transport animals.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of exchange exists; value is stored in social obligation and remembered reciprocity; deferred exchange operates through gift and counter-gift within known kinship networks; no accounting beyond living memory.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: No surplus to extract; redistribution operates through immediate sharing of kills and gathered resources within the band; no taxation, no tribute, no rent.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Wealth is effectively uniform at near-zero; personal possessions are limited to tools and body ornament; no property to defend beyond immediate camp and carcass.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Knapping debris and butchery waste accumulate at occupation sites; abandoned camps are left to weather; no recycling beyond opportunistic reuse of cores; residue is spatially localized and ecologically trivial.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship remains the sole organizing principle; bands of 20–50 individuals cohere around maternal and paternal lines; inheritance is limited to imitative knowledge and personal tools passed at death; no formal property transfer rules beyond custom.

Association & Mutual Aid: Mutual aid operates within the band and extends to allied neighboring bands; periodic aggregations for mating, resource sharing, and collective hunts thicken inter-band ties; the fabric is thin but persistent, maintained by face-to-face contact and remembered obligation.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in camp maintenance, tool making, and social grooming; children learn through imitative play; no evidence of formal festivity, but group cohesion is maintained through shared activities and physical proximity.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status distinctions are minimal and situational — skilled hunters or knowledgeable elders command deference but not institutionalized authority; no caste, no class, no hereditary rank; incoming modern human bands likely display similar structures, though possibly with tighter social cohesion enabling larger aggregation sizes.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administration exists; decision-making is consensual and ad hoc; leadership is achieved, not ascribed, and lapses with incapacity; no institutional persistence beyond the band itself.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Coercion is interpersonal; no organized violence apparatus; conflict between bands is resolved through avoidance, display, or small-scale skirmishing; weaponry is hunting equipment repurposed — spears, clubs, thrown stones; no fortification, no standing force.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction is discharged through fission — disgruntled individuals or factions split off to join other bands or form new ones; grievance does not accumulate institutionally; the residue is minimal, absorbed by mobility and the small scale of social units.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational — the skilled tracker leads the hunt, the experienced elder guides decisions about camp movement; personal authority rests on demonstrated competence and cannot be delegated or inherited; charisma is local and perishable.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is owed to kin and band, not to abstract authority; legitimacy is immediate and relational, tested daily through provisioning and protection; no ruler exists to command or lose allegiance.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective resolve is episodic — marshaled for hunts, relocations, or defense, then dissipating; no sustained political will exists beyond immediate coordination; the band acts as a unit only when circumstance demands.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands — both archaic and incoming modern — are shaped by resource competition and mating opportunity; posture is opportunistic, shifting between avoidance, exchange, and conflict as conditions change; no sustained rivalry or alliance persists across generations.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: The prevailing temper is cautious vigilance, attuned to environmental threat and inter-band encounter; trust extends fully within the band and tentatively to known neighbors; strangers — including members of the other population — provoke wariness but not automatic hostility; the mood is neither expansive nor fearful, calibrated to immediate circumstance.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection is resolved through departure; apathy is a luxury unavailable to subsistence foragers; spent will is regenerated by rest and success; no standing reservoir of exhaustion accumulates.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: The shared code is imitative gesture supplemented by vocalization — grunts, calls, and possibly proto-linguistic signals; full language is absent or nascent; mutual intelligibility within the band is high, declining sharply with distance and unfamiliarity; incoming Homo sapiens may possess more developed vocal communication, conferring an edge in coordination and knowledge transmission.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Transmission is face-to-face and immediate; information travels no faster than a walking messenger; reach is limited to the band and its immediate neighbors; no broadcast capacity exists.

Record, Storage & Persistence: There is no record beyond living memory; knowledge persists only in the heads of those who carry it; each death risks permanent loss; transmission is oral-imitative, vulnerable to drift and decay.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: No formal censorship exists; discourse norms are implicit, learned through imitation; taboos may govern certain topics, but enforcement is social, not institutional; the permitted band is wide within the limits of the communicative code.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is immediate and undivided; amplification occurs through repetition by high-status individuals; no competing channels vie for attention; signal propagation is slow but high-fidelity within the band.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Noise is low in face-to-face communication; signal integrity degrades across inter-band transmission as messages pass through multiple relays; no verification mechanism exists beyond personal trust; the residue is information loss at the margins.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The sense of justice is intuitive and kin-centered — reciprocity within the band, suspicion of outsiders, punishment of free-riders; fairness is measured by contribution and need; no abstract principles are articulated, but the moral baseline is consistent and enforced.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No codified law exists; binding norms are customary, transmitted through imitation and reinforced by social sanction; evolution is slow, constrained by the limits of non-linguistic transmission.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are adjudicated informally by elders or resolved through direct confrontation; sanction ranges from shaming to ostracism to violence; liability is personal, not inherited; no formal procedure exists.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Rights are implicit in kinship — the right to share in the kill, to protection by band-mates, to a place at the fire; compliance burden is low, embedded in daily routine; no external authority imposes rules.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Impunity is checked by proximity — wrongdoers cannot hide within the small band; unredressed wrong festers into grudge, resolved by fission or violence; the residue is personal, not institutional, and clears with the death or departure of the aggrieved.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry exists; the reigning paradigm is practical — what works is retained, what fails is abandoned; causal understanding is local and empirical, lacking abstraction; the discovery frontier is advanced by accident and accumulated experience.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical method is sophisticated within its limits — prepared-core techniques, Levallois-like reduction sequences, hafting of composite tools; knowledge is embodied in motor routines, transmitted hand-to-hand; innovation is slow, constrained by imitative fidelity.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship — the young learn by watching and copying the skilled; the knowledge stock is held entirely in living practitioners; skill distribution is uneven, concentrated in experienced adults; literacy is absent, the concept meaningless.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays with death; superseded techniques are lost rather than archived; error persists uncorrected until it fails in practice; the residue is the steady attrition of accumulated skill, partially offset by each generation's rediscovery.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Identity is kin-based and immediate — "we are this band, descended from these ancestors, occupying this range"; no written mythos exists, but oral-imitative tradition carries origin stories and ancestral memory across generations; the bedrock is thin, vulnerable to disruption by demographic turnover.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No formal ideology exists; the legitimating narrative is implicit — "this is how we have always done it"; authority is justified by success and seniority, not by appeal to abstract principle.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is functional — tools, hide-working implements, simple ornament; occasional ochre use hints at symbolic behavior; the visual surface is sparse, dominated by natural materials worked to purpose; no monumental expression, no representational art survives from this window in this region.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Forms are stable rather than exhausted; innovation is slow, but stagnation does not register as decay within an imitative regime; meaning is immediate and practical, not subject to hollowing; the residue is minimal.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: The cosmology is animist or proto-animist — the world is populated by forces requiring propitiation; the existential outlook is fatalist-practical, accepting death and hardship as given; no articulated theology exists, but the sacred is present in landscape, animal, and ancestor.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: Ritual is minimal and embedded — ochre application to bodies, possible treatment of the dead, seasonal observances tied to game movements; devotion is collective and situational, not calendrical or institutionalized.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists; doctrinal authority resides in elders who carry sacred knowledge; no priesthood, no temple, no separation of sacred from secular; the sacred is woven into daily life.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: As modern humans enter, their spiritual repertoires encounter and partially blend with archaic traditions; no sharp displacement occurs within this window; syncretism is gradual, unrecorded, and archaeologically invisible; the direction is toward sapiens dominance by window's end.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: No disenchantment occurs; the sacred retains its grip; the existential void is unknown; spiritual need is met by the practices at hand; residue is nil.

docs.title: 200,000 BCE – 100,000 BCE — The Dali Cranium and Archaic Homo sapiens
docs.text: Summary: A snapshot of archaic Homo sapiens in the central Loess Plateau during the late Middle Pleistocene, centered on the Dali cranium from Shaanxi Province. This population exhibits a mosaic of Homo erectus retentions and anatomically modern features — a transitional morphology that emerged within the regional lineage without abrupt replacement. The binding constraint is the imitative transmission of technique: all knowledge of tool-making, foraging, and social coordination passes hand to hand and eye to eye, unable to outlast the living carriers or travel faster than a walking group.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Dali site lies on the northeastern fringe of the Loess Plateau in Shaanxi Province, where the Wei River tributary system cuts through thick loess deposits. The surrounding terrain is gently rolling loess uplands dissected by seasonal gullies, with the Qinling Mountains forming a climatic barrier to the south. Movement is channeled along river terraces and through natural passes; cross-plateau travel imposes significant friction, limiting contact radii to adjacent drainage basins.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The window spans portions of Marine Isotope Stages 7 through 5, encompassing a full glacial-interglacial swing. During interglacials, warm-temperate deciduous forest expands across the plateau; glacials push steppe-grassland southward and lower temperatures by several degrees. Precipitation remains monsoon-dominated but highly variable, creating alternating wetter and drier phases that shift resource distributions and seasonal foraging ranges.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: The plateau faces episodic loess slope failures during heavy monsoon rains and periodic droughts during weakened monsoon phases. Seismic activity from the Qinling fault system produces occasional ground shaking. Dust storms during glacial and transitional phases blanket the landscape. Populations maintain mobility as the primary buffer against localized hazard impact.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The loess-derived soils support productive grassland and forest-edge ecotones rich in ungulates (deer, wild cattle, horses) and tubers. Rivers yield freshwater mollusks and fish. Lithic raw material — quartzite cobbles and chert nodules — is locally available in stream gravels and exposed outcrops, though quality varies by locality. The endowment is adequate for small mobile groups but thinly distributed, requiring wide-ranging movement.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Human population densities remain vanishingly low; waste generation consists of organic refuse, fire ash, and lithic debitage dispersed across temporary camps. The landscape absorbs these discharges without measurable accumulation. No residue accretes at scales detectable beyond the immediate campsite.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Endemic parasites from freshwater and undercooked meat impose chronic background loads; injuries from hunting and falls remain common mortality sources. Infant and juvenile mortality is high, driven by infection, malnutrition during lean seasons, and accidental trauma. Life expectancy at birth likely sits below thirty years, with few individuals surviving past forty.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The Dali cranium shows robust bone development consistent with adequate protein intake during growth. Dental wear patterns indicate a mixed diet of tough plant foods and meat. Physiological vitality is sufficient to support large brain size (approximately 1,120 cc) and sustained mobility, though nutritional stress remains episodic during seasonal bottlenecks.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: All healing is social: group members tend wounds with pressure, binding, and medicinal plant application learned by imitation. No specialized healer role exists beyond elder experience. Recovery from moderate injury depends on group tolerance of temporarily reduced mobility; severe trauma is often fatal without intervention capacity.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Reproductive maturity arrives in the mid-teens; pair-bonding patterns remain behaviorally flexible, likely involving serial monogamy within small bands. Female reproductive output is constrained by extended lactation and high infant mortality, keeping net fertility modest despite physiological capacity.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is sparse — perhaps one person per fifty to one hundred square kilometers in favorable zones, far lower in marginal areas. Replacement is barely met; groups persist at small scale (fifteen to thirty individuals) with occasional inter-group contact for mating. Migration flows slowly outward from core territories during favorable periods, contracting during climatic stress.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: Dependent individuals — the very young, injured, and aged — are carried within band tolerance limits. Extended dependency beyond walking capacity is rarely sustainable; the attrition overhang is managed through abandonment or accelerated mortality in crisis periods. The residue is absorbed through group turnover rather than accumulation.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Subsistence depends on opportunistic hunting of medium and large ungulates, plant gathering, and seasonal exploitation of fish and mollusks. The provisioning floor is close to the edge: a failed hunt or drought-stressed plant community translates directly into caloric deficit. Household pooling across kin minimizes individual shortfall risk.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy is captured entirely through human muscle — walking, carrying, throwing, striking — augmented by controlled fire for warmth, cooking, and predator deterrence. Fire use is routine, as evidenced by ash and burned bone at contemporaneous sites. Per-capita work output is limited by caloric intake and physiological endurance.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor is organized by sex-age division: adults of both sexes forage, with males typically undertaking higher-risk hunting and females more intensive plant collection and childcare. No coercion exists beyond social sanction; cooperation is voluntary, reinforced by kin obligation and shared consumption norms.

Production & Surplus Capacity: No surplus accumulates beyond immediate consumption; production capacity exactly meets subsistence needs on average, with deficit periods absorbed through mobility and reduced intake. The concept of stored surplus does not apply to this economy.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No storage technology exists. Body fat serves as the only reserve; lean seasons draw down physiological buffers rather than material stockpiles. Risk is pooled through sharing obligations within the band.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange consists of meat sharing and reciprocal access to gathering territories. No inter-regional trade networks exist; raw material acquisition is direct, requiring movement to source locations. Logistics is foot-borne, limited by carrying capacity and walking range.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No abstract value medium exists. Obligation is encoded in social memory: individuals who share today hold claims on future returns from recipients. These deferred reciprocity obligations are tracked mentally within small groups and transmitted through imitation of giving behavior.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: No surplus extraction mechanism exists; redistribution is direct sharing of kills and gathered food within the band. Allocation decisions are made collectively in the moment, without institutional mediation.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Personal possessions are limited to a few stone tools, hides, and carrying containers. No wealth concentration or asset defense strategies exist; abandonment of material goods is routine during movement.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Lithic debitage, bone fragments, and ash are left at campsites and dispersed naturally. No waste management practice exists; the residue is negligible at population densities prevailing.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Kinship is traced through both parents in overlapping networks; residence is flexible, with individuals moving between bands based on marriage and resource conditions. Inheritance consists of behavioral transmission — technique and territory knowledge — rather than material property, passing through imitation from parent to offspring and elder to junior.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the sole association, encompassing all mutual aid. Cooperation in hunting, food sharing, childcare, and defense against predators is normative. No formal associations exist beyond kin-structured bands; inter-band contact is episodic and governed by negotiated reciprocity.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in rest, grooming, play among juveniles, and social bonding around fire. No formalized leisure structure exists; sociability is continuous and embedded in daily activity rather than partitioned into distinct time-use categories.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status differentiation is minimal; older individuals with greater experience command informal deference, and skilled hunters gain prestige, but no hereditary or fixed stratification exists. Group structure is egalitarian in material terms, with status contingent on demonstrated competence and generosity.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists. Decision-making is collective and situational, achieved through face-to-face discussion, imitation of successful leaders, and consensus. No offices, records, or formal procedures structure authority.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: No specialized coercive apparatus exists. All adults are armed for hunting and capable of violence; conflict resolution depends on social sanction, avoidance, and fission of groups under irreconcilable tension. Homicide and expulsion are possible but unorganized.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through band fission, individual departure, and conflict resolution by dominant individuals. Grievance does not accumulate institutionally; it resolves or causes group splitting. No apparatus can decay because none exists to ossify. The residue is minimal and transient.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational, concentrated in individuals with proven skill in specific domains — a successful hunter leads the hunt, an elder with plant knowledge guides foraging. No permanent authority exists; personal pull derives from demonstrated competence and cannot be inherited or formalized.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is direct and personal — loyalty to kin and band-mates rather than to any abstract order. Legitimacy is continuously enacted through sharing, cooperation, and presence; defection dissolves it instantly. No reservoir of abstract legitimacy exists to draw upon in crisis.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective will forms around immediate survival tasks: the hunt, camp movement, defense against threats. Mobilization is achieved through imitation and emotional contagion — when one acts, others follow. No contested succession or power struggle exists because no permanent office is at stake.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands are cautious, ranging from avoidance through negotiated exchange to episodic violence. Territorial defense is flexible; intrusion provokes confrontation if detected, but boundaries are permeable. No alliance structures exist beyond temporary cooperation during large-game drives.
