Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Sentiment within the band oscillates with subsistence success and interpersonal harmony. Trust is high within kin-close groups, falling sharply toward strangers. Baseline risk perception is elevated: vigilance against predators, rival groups, and environmental hazard is constant. The mood is pragmatic and keyed to immediate conditions.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Spent will manifests as reduced participation, withdrawal, or departure from the band. Apathy does not accumulate institutionally but resolves through individual exit. Disaffection feeds group fission rather than internal disorder. The residue is cleared through mobility.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: The shared code is pre-linguistic: gesture, vocalization, facial expression, and bodily demonstration transmit meaning. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band, declining with distance and unfamiliarity. Complex instruction proceeds by showing, not telling; the bandwidth of imitation is narrow, requiring co-presence and repetition.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Transmission is face-to-face and real-time; nothing travels faster than a walking messenger. Spatial reach is limited to a few days' walk; information beyond that horizon arrives only through inter-band contact at seasonal aggregation points. No amplification exists beyond shouting distance.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists. All information persists in living memory alone; when an individual dies, their knowledge is lost unless already transmitted to others through imitation. Retrieval depends on the presence of a carrier. The record is maximally fragile.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Framing is situational and personal; no institutional censorship exists. Conversational norms are enforced socially through approbation and exclusion. What can be communicated is limited by the gestural-imitative code rather than by prohibition.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Reception is direct; attention follows immediate relevance — danger signals, food discovery, social interaction. No amplification mechanism exists beyond imitation: a useful behavior spreads only as fast as individuals can observe and copy it.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is high within the small group — direct observation minimizes distortion. Drift accumulates across generations as each imitator introduces small errors. No verification mechanism exists to correct accumulated drift; fidelity depends on repetition and redundancy of demonstration.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: The sense of justice is intuitive and reciprocity-based: those who share deserve to receive; cheaters and free-riders merit exclusion or punishment. Fairness is felt directly in the emotional reaction to perceived violation, not articulated in explicit principle.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No codified law exists. Conduct is governed by custom transmitted through imitation — what is done is what should be done. Regulatory evolution occurs slowly, through gradual behavioral drift rather than deliberate reform.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved through direct negotiation, intervention by respected elders, or combat. Liability is assigned by collective judgment in the moment; sanction ranges from public shaming through exclusion to physical punishment. No formal procedure governs adjudication.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is high within normative bounds; compliance burden is minimal — conformity to sharing norms and participation in collective tasks. Rights are not articulated but are enacted through reciprocal treatment.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Impunity exists for the strong or for violations not witnessed. Wrongs may go unredressed when the victim lacks allies or the perpetrator holds social capital. The gap between justice owed and delivered is managed through avoidance and exit rather than accumulated grievance.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry exists. Understanding of the world is practical and embedded in technique — knowing how to knap a stone, track an animal, find water. Causal reasoning is intuitive and associative; no explanatory paradigm is articulated as such.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical method is sophisticated within a narrow range: prepared-core reduction techniques appear at some sites, indicating multi-step planning transmitted through imitation. Tool design shows regional variation, suggesting localized traditions maintained by copying within lineages.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is apprenticeship by observation: juveniles watch adults and imitate, corrected by guidance and repetition. The knowledge stock is distributed across all adults with specialization by aptitude rather than role. Skill attrition through death of carriers is continuous.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Obsolete techniques are shed slowly as practitioners die without transmitting them. Knowledge decay is constant: each generation's stock is a subset of the previous, filtered by transmission success. Error accumulates without external correction.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: Identity is band-based and immediate — we are those who live together, share meat, and know each other's faces. No foundational narrative is articulated in language; origin is enacted through presence and lineage rather than told. Memory reaches back only as far as living recall.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No explicit ideology legitimates the order. The way things are done is self-justifying through repetition: this is how we do it because we have always done it. Legitimacy is habit rather than argument.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture consists of utilitarian objects: stone tools, hides, bone implements. No clearly symbolic artifacts are recovered from the Dali context; aesthetic expression, if present, is perishable or indistinguishable from function. The made-object world is sparse and practical.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Form exhaustion does not apply in the absence of elaborated symbolic forms. Meaning is immediate and situational; no accumulated symbolic repertoire exists to hollow out. The residue is a static baseline rather than a depleted stock.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: Cosmology is implicit — the world is inhabited by animals, plants, weather, and other humans, all encountered directly. No articulated metaphysics distinguishes natural from supernatural; existential questions are not formulated because the cognitive and communicative apparatus to pose them is not yet developed.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No unambiguous ritual practice is evidenced in the material record. If proto-ritual exists, it is behaviorally indistinguishable from routine social action. Devotion, if felt, leaves no recoverable trace.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists. No doctrine is articulated or transmitted. Authority in spiritual matters, if any, is personal and situational, indistinguishable from prestige in other domains.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Spiritual belief, to the extent it exists, is local and stable — no mechanism for diffusion, syncretism, or displacement operates beyond the slow drift of imitation across generations. Nothing is recorded or transmitted beyond immediate contact.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: Disenchantment does not apply where enchantment has not been articulated. The sacred, if present, is immanent in ordinary experience rather than a distinct domain that could be lost. No residue of eroded transcendence accumulates.

docs.title: 1,000,000 BCE – 700,000 BCE — The Lantian Hominins and Early Homo erectus
docs.text: Summary: A static snapshot of early Homo erectus populations occupying the Wei River drainage in Shaanxi Province during the late Early Pleistocene, documented by the Gongwangling cranium (~1.15 Ma) and Chenjiawo mandible (~0.65 Ma), along with associated lithic assemblages preserving Oldowan-like core-and-flake technology. The binding constraint is imitative knowledge transmission: everything the group knows about toolmaking, foraging, and survival resides in living heads and passes only through direct demonstration, hand guiding hand. No verbal instruction, no recorded technique, no external memory exists; knowledge cannot outlast the individuals who carry it. The Lantian hominins represent the southwestern frontier of early Homo erectus expansion into China, adapted to the temperate continental environment of the Loess Plateau margin where the Wei River cuts through the Qinling foothills.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: The Lantian sites lie in the Wei River valley of central Shaanxi, where the river emerges from the Qinling Mountains and flows eastward across the Guanzhong Basin toward its confluence with the Yellow River. Gongwangling sits on an elevated loess terrace north of the modern town; Chenjiawo lies approximately 20 km to the northeast. The Qinling range to the south creates a major orographic barrier, separating the temperate north from the subtropical Yangtze drainage. The Wei corridor provides the primary east-west transit route through central China; north-south movement is channeled by river valleys cutting through the dissected loess terrain.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The late Early Pleistocene climate regime follows 41-kyr orbital cycles, with moderate amplitude oscillations between cooler-drier and warmer-wetter phases. The Lantian area lies at the northern margin of East Asian monsoon influence; monsoon penetration determines the balance between forest and grassland vegetation. During the Gongwangling interval (~1.15 Ma), conditions are relatively warm, supporting mixed deciduous-coniferous forest with open woodland patches. By the Chenjiawo interval (~0.65 Ma), climate has shifted toward cooler, more variable conditions as the Mid-Pleistocene Transition approaches.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: The loess terrain is susceptible to catastrophic erosion during intense rainfall, producing debris flows and gully collapse. Seismic activity along the Weihe Graben poses additional hazard; the region lies within an active tectonic zone. Severe winter cold adds seasonal stress; temperatures drop well below freezing for extended periods.

Resource & Energy Endowment: Raw material for stone tools derives from river gravels — quartzite, vein quartz, and occasional fine-grained volcanic cobbles transported by the Wei and its tributaries. Quality is variable; the best material requires selective collection along gravel bars. Water is available year-round from the Wei River and its tributaries; the valley floor provides access to diverse plant and animal resources.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Loess accumulation buries and preserves archaeological deposits; the Gongwangling cranium was recovered from a thick loess sequence overlying river gravels. Anthropogenic impact is negligible; population densities are far too low to modify the landscape.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Hominin mortality is shaped by trauma, predation, climate exposure, and endemic parasites. The temperate continental climate reduces vector-borne disease pressure but imposes cold-season physiological stress. Life expectancy is short; the Gongwangling cranium represents an adult female who died in early adulthood or middle age.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: The Lantian hominins show robust Homo erectus morphology: the Gongwangling cranium exhibits a low, elongated braincase (~780 cc), heavy supraorbital torus, and thick cranial vault — features consistent with a population adapted to high physical activity and variable food supply. Associated fauna include Stegodon, Equus, Rhinoceros, and various cervids, indicating a mixed grassland-woodland environment with diverse prey species. Dietary reconstruction suggests a broad omnivorous strategy.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healing capacity is limited to the body's regenerative processes and whatever incidental care group proximity affords. The survival of individuals into adulthood, despite the hazards of the environment, suggests some degree of group support, but no direct evidence of deliberate medical treatment survives.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Reproductive biology follows Homo erectus patterns: prolonged juvenile dependency, extended interbirth intervals, and probable cooperative breeding with multi-adult investment in offspring. Sexual dimorphism is moderate, consistent with variable mating systems.

Demographic Renewal & Density: Population density is extremely low. The rarity of hominin fossils across a three-hundred-thousand-year window — two individuals from the Lantian area — reflects both taphonomic loss and genuinely sparse occupation. Bands likely numbered fifteen to thirty individuals, with home ranges spanning hundreds of square kilometers. Local populations are vulnerable to extinction during adverse phases, with recolonization dependent on dispersal from distant groups.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: High infant and juvenile mortality absorbs most reproductive output. Few individuals survive past the fourth decade; the dependency load is modest but rises sharply during resource shortfalls.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Provisioning combines plant gathering, scavenging, and opportunistic hunting. The associated faunal assemblage at Lantian includes large mammals — Stegodon, Equus, Rhinoceros — whose bones show evidence of hominin modification, though whether through primary hunting or scavenging is unclear. Smaller prey and plant foods likely constitute the bulk of caloric intake. Stone tools extend access to marrow and adhering tissue, widening the subsistence floor.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Energy derives from human muscle and possibly controlled fire, though direct evidence of fire use at Lantian sites is ambiguous. The temperate climate makes fire advantageous for warmth, cooking, and predator deterrence, but no structured hearths are documented. Per-capita energy throughput remains at the hominin baseline.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Division of labor is minimal, likely structured by age and sex. No coercion beyond immediate dominance interactions exists; cooperation is kin-based and reciprocal.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is confined to stone tools — simple cores, unretouched flakes, and occasional choppers — and perishable items. The lithic assemblages are Oldowan-like: expedient, unstandardized, produced as needed. No surplus accumulation exists.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No food storage technology exists. Body fat reserves and cached carcass parts are the only buffers, lasting days at most. Winter scarcity poses recurring stress.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Exchange is limited to immediate sharing within the band. Raw material transport extends a few kilometers; no evidence of inter-band trade exists.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: Deferred reciprocity within kin networks is the only form of value storage. No symbolic tokens or standardized medium exist.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Redistribution operates through face-to-face sharing at the moment of acquisition. No formalized extraction apparatus exists.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Material inequality is absent. Personal possessions are limited to tools in hand; there is nothing to defend.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Knapping debris, broken tools, and food refuse are abandoned in place, buried by loess accumulation. No waste routing exists; the residue is absorbed by natural sedimentation.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: The band is structured by kinship, likely with female philopatry and male dispersal. Inheritance is social: children inherit access to kin networks and proximity to skill-holders, not material property.

Association & Mutual Aid: The band is the primary associational unit. Mutual aid obligations bind members through sharing and coalitional support. No inter-band institutions exist; encounters with other groups are episodic and unstructured.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Rest periods afford grooming and juvenile play, serving socialization and motor-skill development. No material correlates of leisure activities survive.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Status hierarchy is informal, based on age, sex, and individual attributes. No institutionalized stratification exists.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: Formal administration is absent. Coordination arises from immediate signals, leadership by example, and learned movement patterns.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Coercion is limited to individual aggression using body and opportunistic objects. No organized weaponry or collective violence apparatus exists.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Social friction discharges through dominance interaction, submission, reconciliation, and emigration. The band is too small to accumulate institutional decay; the residue clears with each generation.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational, arising from demonstrated competence rather than fixed office. Authority is personal and task-specific.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance is personal and immediate, tied to kinship and familiarity. No abstract authority exists.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is limited to coordinated foraging, predator response, and group movement. The band cannot mobilize for sustained collective projects.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other bands are wary, ranging from avoidance to aggression. No stable alliances or organized enmities exist.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Behavioral temper is cautious, shaped by predation pressure and environmental uncertainty. Trust is narrow, extending to close kin and familiar band members.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Disaffection manifests as emigration or marginalization. The band is too small for collective apathy to accumulate; spent will clears through dispersal.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication is pre-linguistic: gesture, vocalization, facial expression, postural cue. The shared code allows coordination and imitative learning but excludes symbolic content or displaced reference. Mutual intelligibility is high within the band.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at walking speed through face-to-face encounter. Knowledge of distant events depends on mobile individuals who have witnessed them.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists. All knowledge — toolmaking, foraging routes, hazard recognition — resides in living memory. The persistence of technique across generations depends entirely on continuous demonstration; any break in the transmission chain erases the knowledge permanently.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: Framing is limited to attentional cues. No propositional discourse, explicit prohibition, or censorship exists.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Reception depends on proximity and focused attention during demonstration. No mechanism for amplification beyond direct perception exists.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is maintained by functional feedback: techniques that produce working tools are copied, others abandoned. Drift accumulates across generations but slowly; the system preserves but cannot improve.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Proto-moral intuitions — reciprocity expectations, aversion to cheating, distress at unfair distribution — are present but implicit. Enforcement is immediate and personal.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No law or codified rule exists. Behavioral norms are transmitted through observation and corrective response.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved through dominance, submission, or avoidance. No third-party adjudication exists.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: Individual autonomy is constrained by group context. Protections derive from kinship, not formal rights.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Wrongs exceeding the victim's retaliatory capacity go unaddressed. Impunity clears through mortality; no accumulated justice deficit persists beyond living memory.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: There is no inquiry in the propositional sense. Understanding is procedural, embedded in motor routines and perceptual skills. Knowledge of raw material properties, animal behavior, and seasonal patterns is practical and implicit.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: The lithic assemblages associated with the Lantian hominins are Oldowan-like: simple core reduction, hard-hammer percussion, expedient flake production. Knappers select cobbles from river gravels, strike to produce sharp-edged flakes, and discard cores when exhausted. No prepared-core techniques, no standardized tool forms, no bifacial working appears. The technology is effective for basic cutting and scraping tasks but represents the Lower Paleolithic baseline.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Skill transmission is purely imitative. Novices learn by watching skilled practitioners and copying their gestures; no verbal instruction, no explicit pedagogy exists. Knowledge stock is distributed unevenly: master knappers hold technique that novices must acquire through proximity. The knowledge cannot be externalized, stored, or retrieved.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge loss is catastrophic. If the band's skilled knappers die without transmitting their techniques, the knowledge vanishes. The residue is discontinuity — populations that fail and recolonizers who must rediscover or reimport what was lost.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: There is no mythos. Group identity is experiential, tied to familiar individuals and places. Memory spans living generations; there is no narrative tradition, no preserved history.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No legitimating narrative exists. The social order requires no justification because there is no capacity to articulate alternatives.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is limited to expedient stone tools and perishable objects. No evidence of decoration, symmetry imposed for aesthetic purposes, or symbolic marking survives. Form follows function and raw material constraint.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: Without symbolic content, there is no meaning to exhaust. Tool forms persist unchanged because the imitative system conserves without innovating; the residue is stasis.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No cosmology exists in any recoverable sense. The world is encountered directly, without explanatory framework or metaphysical overlay.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: There is no evidence of ritual or sacred practice. Behavior is instrumental; no distinction between practical and sacred activity can be identified.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: Religious institutions are absent. No doctrine, hierarchy, or sacred office exists.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: Without spiritual content, there is nothing to diffuse, blend, or displace.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: There is no enchantment to lose. The imitative substrate cannot generate or transmit cosmological propositions; the spiritual dimension is blank.

docs.title: 780,000 BCE – 400,000 BCE — Zhoukoudian Locality 1 and Peking Man
docs.text: Summary: A limestone cave system on the northern China plain serves as a recurrent occupation site for Homo erectus populations over nearly four hundred thousand years; the binding constraint is the cave's singular concentration of shelter, water proximity, and faunal access in an otherwise exposed landscape, which channels hominin presence into this narrow locale and accumulates the deepest erectus record in East Asia.

docs.title: D01. Physical Domain
docs.text:
Geography & Spatial Friction: Locality 1 sits at Dragon Bone Hill, a limestone outlier of the Western Hills forty kilometers southwest of modern Beijing, where karstic dissolution has carved a fissure complex into the escarpment facing the Zhoukoudian River valley; the cave opens east, shielded from prevailing winter winds, with the valley floor offering access to stream water, game corridors, and the flatter terrain of the North China Plain beyond; movement across the plain is unimpeded, but entry to the Western Hills requires threading passes that funnel transit.

Climate Regime & Volatility: The occupation spans multiple glacial-interglacial oscillations; during cooler phases the region shifts toward steppe-grassland with boreal elements, while warmer interstadials restore temperate deciduous forest; the cave deposits preserve pollen and faunal shifts recording these swings, with the coldest intervals pushing tree lines southward and expanding open habitats favored by large herbivores; monsoon variability alters summer precipitation, affecting stream flow and plant productivity on a decadal scale.

Hazard Regime & Exposure: The cave roof is subject to periodic roof-fall as limestone weathers, depositing blocks that punctuate the stratigraphic sequence; seasonal flooding from the adjacent stream occasionally inundates lower deposits; seismic activity along regional fault systems poses a low-frequency collapse risk; beyond the cave, open grassland exposes occupants to predators and extreme temperature swings.

Resource & Energy Endowment: The limestone provides shelter but no tool-quality stone; hominins procure quartz and quartzite from river gravels and outcrops within a few kilometers; faunal remains indicate abundant large mammals, particularly deer, horses, and rhinoceros, available in the valley and adjacent plains; firewood from surrounding forest or shrubland supplies combustion fuel.

Waste Absorption & Sink Capacity: Butchery debris, ash lenses, and discarded stone accumulate on the cave floor over millennia, raising the surface incrementally; organic decay proceeds slowly in sheltered sediment; the cave functions as a sediment trap, incorporating hominin refuse into the deposit rather than dispersing it; no evidence of systematic waste removal exists, leaving the residue to accrete as the stratigraphic record.

docs.title: D02. Biological Domain
docs.text:
Pathogen Load & Mortality Baseline: Skeletal evidence from multiple individuals shows healed trauma, suggesting survival through injury; endemic parasites and zoonotic exposure from prey handling pose chronic risk; no direct pathogen evidence survives, but proximity to large herbivore carcasses and cave occupation alongside carnivores implies repeated disease exposure; mortality is high, with few individuals surviving past middle adulthood.

Nutrition & Physiological Vitality: Cranial capacity ranges from approximately 850 to 1100 cubic centimeters across recovered specimens, consistent with robust Homo erectus morphology; dental wear patterns indicate a mixed diet of tough plant material and meat; stature and robusticity suggest adequate caloric intake during favorable intervals, though growth stress indicators on teeth imply periodic nutritional shortfall.

Care, Healing & Recovery Capacity: Healed fractures on some specimens indicate survival through significant trauma, implying group tolerance of injured members; no evidence of elaborate wound treatment exists; healing capacity rests on rest, group provisioning, and physiological resilience; the imitative-stage constraint means any care knowledge transmits only through direct demonstration, limiting diffusion beyond immediate kin.

Reproductive Biology & Pairing Dynamics: Population size at any given occupation is small, likely multi-family bands; mating patterns are unrecoverable, but the presence of juveniles in the assemblage implies local reproduction; sexual dimorphism consistent with polygynous or flexible mating systems; no direct evidence of pair-bond structure survives.

Demographic Renewal & Density: The site accumulates remains of at least forty individuals across the occupation span, representing episodic use by small groups rather than continuous dense habitation; replacement relies on local births and possible recruitment from neighboring bands; population density across the North China Plain remains very low, with Zhoukoudian serving as one of few known anchor points.

Attrition & Dependency Overhang: High juvenile mortality is inferred from age profiles; dependent elderly are rare in the fossil record, suggesting few survive to advanced age; the productive adult cohort carries the young, but the dependency load is lightened by early death; orphan care beyond weaning is uncertain but consistent with ape-like patterns of extended juvenile dependence.

docs.title: D03. Economic Domain
docs.text:
Subsistence & Provisioning Floor: Subsistence centers on hunting and scavenging large and medium mammals, supplemented by plant foods; faunal assemblages show cut-marked bones of deer, horse, elephant, and rhinoceros; procurement strategies likely combine active hunting with opportunistic access to carnivore kills; the cave concentrates processing activity, with marrow extraction evidenced by bone breakage patterns.

Energy Capture & Conversion: Human muscle provides all motive power; fire use is attested by ash deposits, burned bone, and charred seeds in multiple layers, representing one of the earliest sustained fire records outside Africa; fire extends the energy budget by enabling warmth in cold intervals, extending active hours, and improving digestibility of meat and plant foods; firewood collection imposes labor cost but expands the caloric return on hunted carcasses.

Labor Organization & Coercion: Labor is organized within small multi-family bands; task division by age and sex is plausible but unrecoverable; no evidence of coerced labor exists; cooperation in hunting large prey implies coordinated group effort; sharing of carcasses and fire is likely, given the concentration of processing debris.

Production & Surplus Capacity: Production is limited to immediate consumption; stone tools are manufactured on-site using local quartz and imported quartzite; no evidence of surplus accumulation or delayed consumption beyond short-term caching; the economy operates at the subsistence edge, with output matching intake cycle by cycle.

Storage, Reserves & Buffering: No storage facilities exist; the cave may serve as a short-term cache for carcasses under processing, but preservation is limited to days; fat reserves in hunted animals provide the primary buffer against scarcity; group mobility to alternative resource patches substitutes for fixed storage.

Exchange, Trade & Logistics: Raw material sourcing indicates movement of quartzite from sources five to ten kilometers distant, implying either direct procurement trips or exchange between bands; no formal trade networks exist; logistics are limited to what individuals and groups can carry; the cave's fixed location anchors a home-range pattern of radial foraging.

Value Storage, Credit & Deferred Exchange: No medium of stored value exists; reciprocity operates on immediate or near-term sharing within the band; deferred obligations, if any, are held in memory and transmitted by example; the imitative-stage constraint prevents codification of debts.

Surplus Extraction & Redistribution: Surplus, when it occurs, is redistributed through sharing at the kill or processing site; no extractive hierarchy exists; dominant individuals may claim priority access, but extraction is limited to consumption, not accumulation.

Wealth Distribution & Asset Defense: Personal property is limited to carried tools and perhaps hafted implements; no durable wealth accumulation occurs; defense of the cave site against competing groups or predators may represent the closest analogue to asset defense.

Byproducts & Waste Routing: Butchery refuse, ash, and lithic debitage accumulate in the cave deposit; organic waste decays in place; no systematic disposal occurs; the residue forms the archaeological record, left to accrete without clearance.

docs.title: D04. Social Domain
docs.text:
Kinship, Family & Inheritance: Social organization is inferred as multi-family bands linked by kinship; inheritance of material goods is negligible given the absence of durable property; knowledge and behavioral tendencies transmit through imitation within kin groups; maternal lines likely anchor juvenile rearing.

Association & Mutual Aid: Cooperation extends to hunting, fire maintenance, and site defense; mutual aid within the band is essential for survival; no evidence of inter-band alliances exists, though peaceful encounters at resource patches are plausible; the imitative-stage constraint limits coordination to what can be demonstrated and copied.

Leisure, Play & Sociability: Non-work time is spent in proximity around fire hearths; play among juveniles and social grooming among adults likely reinforce bonds; no artifacts interpretable as recreational survive; sociability is mediated by shared space and warmth.

Stratification, Status & Group Structure: Hierarchy is likely based on age, sex, and physical prowess; no formal status markers survive; dominant individuals may control access to prime meat or sleeping positions; group structure is fluid, with fission-fusion dynamics plausible given the long occupation span.

Administrative Capacity & Institutional Integrity: No administrative apparatus exists; coordination is immediate and face-to-face; leadership, if any, is situational and personal; the band lacks institutional continuity beyond the memory of living members.

Coercive Apparatus & Means of Force: Force is interpersonal; stone tools and fire-hardened sticks serve as weapons for hunting and defense; organized violence against other groups is unattested but plausible; the cave provides defensible shelter against predators and rival bands.

Discharge, Disorder & Decay: Conflict within the band is managed by dominance displays and avoidance; exclusion of troublesome individuals through fission is available; disorder at the inter-band level is mediated by low population density and wide spacing; the social fabric is fragile, dependent on living relationships with no institutional backup.

docs.title: D05. Emotional Domain
docs.text:
Leadership & Personal Authority: Leadership is situational, tied to hunting skill, physical strength, or social acuity; no formal office exists; authority is personal and must be reasserted in each context; the imitative-stage constraint means leadership cannot be delegated or institutionalized.

Legitimacy as Lived Allegiance: Allegiance to the band is lived through daily cooperation and shared sustenance; no abstract legitimating principle exists; loyalty erodes if provisioning fails or conflict escalates, leading to band fission.

Political Will & Collective Resolve: Collective action is episodic, mobilized for specific hunts or site defense; no standing political will persists beyond the task; resolve is generated by immediate need and dissipates when the need passes.

External Relations & Posture: Relations with other groups are infrequent given low population density; encounters may be neutral, competitive, or occasionally hostile; no evidence of sustained alliance or warfare exists; the band's posture is defensive, centered on maintaining access to the cave and its environs.

Public Sentiment & Behavioral Temper: Affective life centers on immediate kin and band-mates; trust extends to familiar faces; strangers are approached with caution; the shared fire creates a focal point for group cohesion; anxiety spikes with predator encounters or resource failure, settling as conditions stabilize.

Disaffection, Apathy & Spent Will: Individual disaffection may lead to departure or expulsion; collective apathy is unlikely given the immediacy of survival demands; spent will after failed hunts or harsh winters may trigger mobility to new ranges rather than settled despair.

docs.title: D06. Informational Domain
docs.text:
Communication Accessibility: Communication relies on gesture, vocalization, facial expression, and demonstration; no evidence of articulate language exists for this population; mutual intelligibility is high within the band, lower with strangers; the imitative-stage constraint limits information transfer to what can be shown and copied.

Channels & Transmission Velocity: Information travels at the speed of physical movement; the band is the information unit; transmission to distant groups occurs only through direct encounter or dispersal of individuals; velocity is slow, measured in kilometers per generation.

Record, Storage & Persistence: No external record exists; knowledge persists only in living memory and embodied skill; loss of knowledgeable individuals erases their knowledge; the fire-use tradition persists across millennia, indicating successful intergenerational transmission through imitation, but each link is fragile.

Framing, Censorship & Discourse Norms: No formal censorship exists; communication norms are set by social hierarchy and attention; dominant individuals may interrupt or redirect; the permitted band of expression is wide but shallow, limited by the absence of symbolic language.

Reception, Attention & Amplification: Attention is captured by immediate stimuli: fire, food, threat, social drama; amplification occurs through repetition and emotional contagion; no mechanism for long-distance signal amplification exists.

Signal Integrity & Noise Load: Signal integrity is high within the band due to face-to-face communication; noise increases with distance and unfamiliarity; verification is immediate and contextual; the imitative-stage constraint means error correction is limited to repeated demonstration.

docs.title: D07. Moral Domain
docs.text:
Moral Foundations & Sense of Justice: Moral sense is rooted in reciprocity, kin preference, and dominance hierarchy; fairness in sharing is likely enforced by emotional reaction to perceived cheating; justice is immediate and personal, not codified.

Law, Codification & Regulatory Evolution: No law exists; behavioral norms are transmitted by example and enforced by social pressure; the imitative-stage constraint prevents codification; norms drift with each transmission.

Adjudication, Liability & Sanction: Disputes are resolved by dominance display, submission, or avoidance; there is no formal adjudication; sanction is immediate, ranging from exclusion to physical punishment; no appeal mechanism exists.

Rights, Protections & Compliance Burden: No abstract rights exist; protection is conferred by membership in the band and by personal relationships; compliance with norms is enforced by social monitoring; the burden is light given the small group size and transparency of behavior.

Impunity & Unredressed Wrong: Dominant individuals may act with relative impunity; redress for wrongs depends on the victim's ability to retaliate or mobilize allies; unredressed grievances may lead to departure or fission; the gap between justice owed and delivered is managed by mobility rather than resolution.

docs.title: D08. Intellectual Domain
docs.text:
Inquiry, Theory & Paradigm: No formal inquiry exists; understanding is practical and immediate; causal reasoning is applied to hunting, fire maintenance, and tool manufacture; no theoretical paradigm separates knowledge from action.

Applied Knowledge & Technical Method: Technical knowledge includes stone flaking, fire-making and maintenance, carcass processing, and shelter use; methods are transmitted by imitation; innovation occurs slowly, with successful variants spreading through copying; the industry shows continuity over hundreds of thousands of years, indicating conservative transmission.

Education, Knowledge Stock & Skill Distribution: Education is informal, occurring through observation and guided practice; the knowledge stock is held in living practitioners; skill distribution is limited to the band; loss of skilled individuals reduces the local stock; no mechanism exists to recover lost knowledge except through independent reinvention or contact with other groups.

Obsolescence & Knowledge Decay: Knowledge decays when transmission chains break; the long persistence of fire use and stone tool traditions indicates robust transmission, but subtle skills may be lost without notice; error accumulates across generations unless corrected by immediate feedback from the environment.

docs.title: D09. Cultural Domain
docs.text:
Mythos, Memory & Foundational Identity: No recoverable mythos exists; identity is grounded in lived experience and kin recognition; memory extends only to the lifespan of individuals; foundational narratives, if any, are enacted rather than recounted.

Legitimating Narrative & Ideology: No explicit ideology exists; the order is legitimated by its persistence and by the dominance of its leaders; no alternative narrative is articulable.

Artistic Expression & Material Culture: Material culture is limited to stone tools, fire hearths, and organic implements that do not survive; no art or ornamentation is attested at Zhoukoudian for this period; the made-object world is functional, with no evident symbolic embellishment.

Form Exhaustion & Meaning Decay: The question of form exhaustion does not apply in the absence of symbolic forms; meaning is immediate and contextual; no residue of hollowed symbols accrues.

docs.title: D10. Spiritual Domain
docs.text:
Cosmology & Existential Outlook: No recoverable cosmology exists; existential orientation is practical and present-focused; the metaphysical frame, if any, is enacted in behavior rather than articulated.

Ritual, Devotion & Sacred Practice: No unambiguous ritual evidence exists; the treatment of the dead is uncertain, with some suggestion of intentional accumulation of crania, but taphonomic processes may account for the pattern; fire use may carry proto-ritual significance, but this is speculative.

Religious Institutions & Doctrinal Authority: No religious institution exists; doctrinal authority is absent; the imitative-stage constraint prevents transmission of abstract belief.

Spiritual Diffusion, Syncretism & Displacement: The question of spiritual diffusion does not apply in the absence of articulated belief; any proto-spiritual orientation is localized and dies with its holders.

Disenchantment & Sacred Discharge: No disenchantment occurs in the absence of enchantment; the sacred, if present, is enacted and immediate, leaving no residue when the actors depart.

docs.title: Manuscript Stage
docs.text: Description: External records kept outside the body become the medium public life runs on — accounts, holdings, and obligations, then laws, letters, and argument, written rather than remembered. Persistence becomes systematic: a record outlasts its maker, can be consulted by someone never told, and accumulates beyond any living memory. The substrate begins as the administrative store of early states and deepens across the stage — as signs detach from the things they pictured into a recombinable script able to set down anything sayable, as literacy spreads beyond the specialist class toward the public, and as cheap, abundant paper carries records through everyday public life. Dominant until mass print carries the public sphere.
